title: History-making Miss USA reveals how she got swimsuit-ready while raising 2 young kids
summary: Justus Kelley reveals how she prepped for the Miss USA pageant during nap times and bath routines while caring for her two young foster children.
story: Justus Kelley shares how she practiced with her baby in a carrier, squeezed in workouts during nap time and prepared for the stage around motherhood.
Justus Kelley made history as the first mother and first married woman to win Miss USA — and she got there in an unconventional way.

On Aug. 27, the organization hosted the 75th edition of the national pageant in Miami. The 31-year-old, who was Miss Virginia USA 2026, succeeded last year’s winner, Audrey Eckert, 24. The pageant opened the competition to married women and mothers in 2023.

"My pageant prep, it did look different," Kelley told Fox News Digital. "I'm not going to pretend like I was able to dedicate the same amount of time as what I did in the past. I had to get creative. Their nap time was my prep time. It was late nights. It was after the bath and bed routine. I did walking classes with my baby on my chest, in his carrier. I did squats in my living room while holding my two-year-old. I practiced interview questions while feeding my toddler."
NAVY VETERAN TRADES MILITARY UNIFORM FOR MISS GEORGIA SASH FOLLOWING HEARTBREAKING LOSS

Miss Virginia USA 2026 Justus Kelley is crowned Miss USA 2026 onstage during the 2026 Miss USA Final Competition & Coronation at Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts on Aug. 27, 2026, in Miami, Florida. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"There were days when I wished I could just take the entire day to dedicate to pageant prep, but that's not where I am," Kelley said. "That's not the season of life that I'm in. And we made it work, and my family was fully on board with this experience. They know that they're along for the journey; they're along for this ride with me."

The Miss USA pageant began in 1952 in Long Beach, California, with New York's Jackie Loughery becoming its first winner. The competition is separate from the Miss America pageant, which traces its history to a 1921 event in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

Miss USA 2026 winner Justus Kelley and Miss Florida Aileen Cerchiara stand on stage during the 2026 Miss USA Final Competition and Coronation at Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Florida., on Aug. 27, 2026. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

Kelley, a foster mom of two, is the first married mother to retain the Miss USA title. In 1957, Mary Leona Gage was crowned Miss USA but was stripped of the title the following day after pageant organizers learned she was married and the mother of two sons.
Mary Leona Gage Ennis, who won the title of Miss USA in the contest and then lost it when it was discovered she was married and the mother of two children, is shown in this 1956 photo. (Getty Images)
WATCH: MISS USA 2026 REVEALS HOW SHE TRAINED FOR PAGEANT WITH KIDS IN TOW
Kelley said she ditched social media and TV in favor of workouts whenever she found a spare moment while caring for her two young children.

"I love abductor and adductor exercises, something that I usually do on a machine at the gym," she explained. "But if I can't make it to the gym, I'm just lying on the floor, elevating my leg and mirroring what I would've done on that machine. For me, leading up to a pageant, knowing there's a fitness component, I'm going to be in a swimsuit on that stage. I want to feel good. I want to show off all this hard work."

Abductor and adductor exercises target opposing muscle groups in your hips and thighs that help control side-to-side movement, stabilize your pelvis, and support balance and overall lower-body stability. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"I really focused on core," she said. "So a lot of times you'll find me at home in the living room. I might be watching a movie or doing some self-care, but I am on the floor crunching it out during that movie, saying, 'Let's try to get through this whole scene doing crunches,' and then you pause. It was really all about focusing on core."

Miss USA 2026 Justus Kelley stands on stage during the Miss USA Final Competition and Coronation at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Florida, on Aug. 27, 2026. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
Kelley said her husband's support also helped her through the competition.

"The crown might be his because all he keeps saying is, 'I can't believe I'm Mr. USA,'" Kelley said with a laugh, referring to her college sweetheart. "I'm like, 'Babe, I don't know if that might be trademarked. Stop saying that!'"
Justus Kelley and her husband are fostering a baby boy and his sister. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"He is so over the moon," Kelley said. "We've been together for 13, going on 14 years and married for nine. He's been a part of every bit of this journey. I've been competing for over 10 years now. And from my very first pageant, he was there holding a sign with my face on it up until the very end. I did not get here alone. He's been a huge supporter. My husband's a consultant, and he's been calling himself my pageant consultant. But he's been a huge help in getting me to this point."

Justus Kelley walks the runway at the Michael Cinco show during New York Fashion Week Powered by Art Hearts Fashion at The Angel Orensanz Foundation on Sept. 12, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images for Art Hearts Fashion)

This year's prize package, valued at more than $685,000, includes a $150,000 salary, a Range Rover, a one-year lease at a luxury Miami apartment, a Westgate Vacation Home Club membership and a $30,000 Miss Universe wardrobe, according to People magazine.

"The prize that made me go, 'Wow, and I have some questions,' was knowing that the Range Rover is a part of traveling in style even after your year as Miss USA. I think that's huge. But my first question was, 'Does it fit car seats?'"
Miss USA 2026 Justus Kelley wants to raise the awareness of providing a loving home to foster children. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
Kelley said she wants her year as Miss USA to challenge the idea that women need to choose between their families, careers and personal dreams.

Miss Virginia USA 2026 Justus Kelley is crowned Miss USA 2026 onstage during the Miss USA Final Competition & Coronation at Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts on Aug. 27, 2026, in Miami, Florida. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"You don't have to choose one part of who you are," Kelley said. "You can be all of who you are. That, to me, is the message. We can embrace every part of who we are. It doesn't take away from the other. It doesn't mean there aren't trade-offs, and there aren't times when we have to lean on our village more heavily to get through all the things that we may be pursuing. But know that we don't have to sacrifice ourselves."

From left: Miss Virginia Justus Kelley, Miss Florida Aileen Cerchiara and Miss Pennsylvania Elizabeth Voight appear on stage during the 2026 Miss USA Final Competition and Coronation at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Florida, on Aug. 27, 2026. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)
Looking ahead, Kelley said her victory wasn't only personal — she also saw it as a chance to represent mothers and wives balancing family life with their own ambitions.

Justus Kelley and her husband Tyler have been licensed foster parents in the Commonwealth of Virginia for nearly two years. (Ivan Apfel/Getty Images)

"Knowing that history was made as the first mom, as the first wife, as the first woman in her 30s, my first thought was how amazing it is to get to do this and to represent women from all over the country, from all over the world that resonate with, 'Hey, we're still dreaming,'" she said.

"We're raising our families, but we still have dreams. We still have things that we want to go after and pursue. But what an honor. I get to do this. I get to represent these women. What an honor."

title: John Ritter's widow Amy Yasbeck details the fatal misdiagnosis she says led to his death
summary: Amy Yasbeck reveals John Ritter was misdiagnosed with a heart attack the night he died, when a CT scan could have detected his aortic dissection.
story: The John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Heath CEO Meredith Ford O'Neal explains why the beloved sitcom star's sudden death resonated with millions and helped raise awareness about aortic dissection.
John Ritter's widow Amy Yasbeck is opening up about the actor's final hours more than two decades after his death.
In September 2003, Ritter died at the age of 54 after suffering an acute aortic dissection, a tear in the inner layer of the aorta, the body's largest artery that delivers blood away from the heart.

Ahead of Aortic Dissection Awareness Week and what would have been Ritter's 78th birthday on Sept. 17, Yasbeck, who founded the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health, and the actor's son, Tyler Ritter, who serves on its board, joined Fox News Digital for an interview.
CARLY PEARCE SAYS HEART CONDITION LEFT HER FEARING A HEART ATTACK: ‘IS MY HEART OK?’
John Ritter's widow, Amy Yasbeck, recalled how he was misdiagnosed with a heart attack before dying of an aortic dissection.  (Getty Images)
Looking back on her husband's death, Yasbeck recalled how Ritter was mistakenly treated for a heart attack after arriving at the hospital, which she said "led to what eventually happened."
"John was sadly misdiagnosed on the night he passed away," Yasbeck said.

"And they didn't do any imaging, but he looked like the guy — right age, right weight, everything — to have a heart attack, and he had chest pain," she continued. "So they just started loading him up with blood thinners and stuff."

"And this is sad because it was the opposite. It wasn't a block in his heart, it was a tear in his aorta, so everything they did that night led to what eventually happened," Yasbeck said. "Because there are ways, once it starts dissecting, if you get to the hospital in time, your chances are way better of living."
John Ritter is seen at CBS TV City on Jan. 5, 1978, in Los Angeles, California. (Tom Wargacki/WireImage)
Following Ritter's death, Yasbeck filed a wrongful death lawsuit alleging Ritter's aortic dissection was misdiagnosed. In 2008, a jury found in favor of the two physicians remaining in the case.
WATCH: JOHN RITTER'S DEATH HIT SO HARD BECAUSE ‘YOU FELT LIKE YOU KNEW HIM’: FOUNDATION CEO

To mark Aortic Dissection Awareness Week, which runs from Sept. 13 to 19, the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health, is launching its "50 for 50" campaign, encouraging supporters to donate $50 while drawing attention to the fact that up to 50% of people who suffer an aortic dissection die before reaching medical care.

Yasbeck told Fox News Digital that she believes annual estimates of aortic dissections likely undercount the number of cases because patients who die before arriving at a hospital often are not included in the data. She said that improving awareness of the condition is one of the most effective ways to reduce those deaths.

However, Yasbeck emphasized that raising awareness is not just for patients and families. She pointed out the importance of ensuring doctors recognize that chest pain can signal an aortic dissection, not just a heart attack.
COUNTRY STAR ASHLEY COOKE SPEAKS OUT ABOUT RARE HEART CONDITION THAT COULD END HER LIFE AT ANY MOMENT
Yasbeck founded the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health after the actor's death.  (WireImage)
"Your heart can be in perfect shape," she said. "You can be an athlete."

"And if the blood that's being pumped into your aorta is going inside the layers of the aorta, instead of being traveled to all of the rest of the highway where it's supposed to go, it's curtains for you," she continued.

"So it's so important to be able to have that awareness," Yasbeck added. "And there's no drug for aortic dissection at this point in time. For blood pressure, which sometimes can help you if you are at risk, right? Keep your blood pressure down, but there's no instant fix for it. You have to be a participant in your own health in this regard. And by doing that, you are also protecting your family. For generations, actually."

Yasbeck said she recently witnessed firsthand how her husband's story has become part of emergency medicine. She recalled accompanying a friend with chest pain to the hospital where medical staff told her they were ordering a CT scan to check for "the John Ritter thing" to rule out an aortic dissection.
Yasbeck explained that Ritter's case has become part of emergency medicine.  (FilmMagic, Inc)

"They said, 'We're checking for the John Ritter thing', not knowing who I am, not knowing whom my friend is that was a friend of John's," she remembered. "It was just like this relief came over me. And my buddy, you know, gave me the thumbs up."

"The fact that they said checking for that ‘John Ritter thing,’ talking shorthand to me, I freaking love that. Call it whatever you want. CT scan, a CAT scan, is the gold standard for diagnosing in an emergency situation, in any situation, but to be able to realize as soon as you can, ‘This is not a heart attack. This is an aortic dissection,’" she continued. "'Fix this a whole different way.'"
'GAME OF THRONES' STAR EMILIA CLARKE WAS CONVINCED SHE 'CHEATED DEATH' AFTER SURVIVING TWO BRAIN ANEURYSMS
While speaking with Fox News Digital, Yasbeck shared that doctors and researchers had told her for years that Ritter's death marked a turning point in awareness of aortic dissection.
"There was kind of a pre-John Ritter awareness of aortic dissection and a post," she said. "Sadly, John died in the last hours of pre-John Ritter awareness."
WATCH: JOHN RITTER'S LEGACY IS HELPING PREVENT DEADY AORTIC DISSECTIONS, DOCTOR SAYS

Since Ritter's death, the "Three's Company" star's family has worked through the John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health to raise awareness about thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections. A thoracic aortic aneurysm is an enlargement of the body's main artery that can often be detected through screening before it tears into an aortic dissection, a life-threatening emergency.

Ritter's widow and his children have encouraged people to learn about their family medical history and seek appropriate screening when they are at increased risk because thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections can have a genetic component.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
John Ritter, seen with Joyce DeWitt and Suzanne Somers, was known for his role on "Three's Company." (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

Yasbeck said doctors now believe Ritter's father likely died from an undiagnosed aortic dissection, while routine screenings after his death revealed the same condition in his brother Tom, allowing him to undergo life-saving surgery before it became fatal.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Tyler, 41, told Fox News Digital that becoming aware of his family history in the aftermath of his father's death had changed his approach to his own health. Ritter shared Tyler as well as son Jason Ritter, 46, and daughter Carly Ritter, 44, with his first wife, actress Nancy Morgan. Yasbeck, who was Ritter's second wife, shared son Noah Ritter, 28.

Amy Yasbeck, John Ritter, Carly Ritter, Tyler Ritter and Jason Ritter attend the premiere of "101 Dalmatians II: Patch's London Adventure" at El Capitan Theater in Hollywood, Calif., United States. (WireImage)

"It's impossible not to imagine that there's a parallel universe where the family demanded an autopsy on our grandfather and discovered an aortic dissection, which led to my dad and his brother getting screened," Tyler said. "And as we see with Tommy, as Amy just said, Tommy is still alive and doing great."

"It's just too easy to imagine that in this other universe, where my grandfather was properly diagnosed, that my dad would be totally fine right now with just an aortic replacement surgery," he continued. "And that, on the one hand, is very difficult to accept and to comprehend."

"On the other hand, it has provided a massive silver lining," Tyler added. "I get scanned every year. My kids know I get scanned. They know why I get scanned. They know that my dad was the last one in our family. Our mission is that he is the last in our family to suffer a dissection."
Amy Yasbeck and Tyler Ritter attend The John Ritter Foundation for Aortic Health's "An Evening From the Heart LA" at Sunset Room Hollywood on May 9, 2024, in Los Angeles, Calif. (Getty Images)
Tyler said watching his own children discover their grandfather through episodes of "Three's Company" has reinforced the importance of preserving Ritter's legacy through awareness.

He explained that though aneurysms are often asymptomatic, they can be detected through screening, which is why he encourages families with a history of aortic disease or unexplained early deaths to speak with their doctors.

"The more you know," he said. "If you can spot in a first-degree relative that there's a potential for a missed or undiagnosed illness or disease, it would just be worth asking your doctor."
Looking back, Tyler said his father's death remains a tragedy, but one that has helped protect other families.

title: Jennifer Aniston’s romance with Jim Curtis faces celebrity relationship trap, expert warns
summary: Matchmaker Gina Hendrix says Jennifer Aniston may be making classic celebrity relationship mistakes with boyfriend Jim Curtis by trying to build him up.
story: Professional matchmaker Gina Hendrix explains why the 'Friends' star might be making a classic mistake in her relationship.

Jennifer Aniston’s relationship with hypnotherapist and life coach Jim Curtis has gotten serious in the more than a year and a half since they started dating, but a matchmaker worries the "Friends" star could be making classic mistakes as the higher-profile partner.

"I think one of the biggest mistakes is when a woman tries to kind of manage the guy," Los Angeles-based matchmaker Gina Hendrix told Fox News Digital. "When a woman steps into this role, and it's always a great, successful, amazing woman, she thinks, ‘I did it for myself, I can do it for you too,’ and she tries to build the guy up."

Hendrix warned that the guy often "ends up with all this new great life, but then he resents her for the help, and she takes on a very unsexy role, and then usually it just all fizzles out from there."
JENNIFER ANISTON’S BOYFRIEND, JIM CURTIS, REVEALS WHAT 'FRIENDS' STAR IS REALLY LIKE BEHIND CLOSED DOORS
Jennifer Aniston and Jim Curtis are seen together at an event in 2025. (Getty Images for ELLE)
She said it takes an "incredibly secure person" to date a celebrity and "share that kind of spotlight, but still be out of the spotlight to keep this relationship afloat."

It’s always better to "keep your relationship out of the public eye as much as humanly possible for so many reasons, and if you can live a life where it's under the radar, and you can live a life that is as private as you could possibly have," she added.
THOMAS RHETT REVEALS WHY HE AND WIFE LAUREN REJECT CELEBRITY PERKS FOR COUNTRY LIFE
Hendrix said she appreciates it when celebrity spouses avoid red carpet events. "You really should just keep it out, keep it away as far as you can" from the public eye, she added.
"I think one of the biggest mistakes is when a woman tries to kind of manage the guy."

MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SHOCKS WITH 15-YEAR CELIBACY CONFESSION AS SHARON STONE, TERI HATCHER RETHINK ROMANCE
Jennifer Aniston interviewed Jim Curtis at an event for his new book earlier this month. (Brie Stimson/Fox News Digital)
MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY'S PIECE OF RELATIONSHIP ADVICE THAT KEEPS HIS MARRIAGE TO CAMILA ALVES STRONG
The key to a successful relationship involving a celebrity who has "kind of souped up their partner" is "mutual respect," she said.

"You have to be with somebody that, you know, that you want their opinion. You value how they think," she said. "And I think beyond the typical things of attraction and the butterflies in the stomach and the great sex and all these things, you also have to respect this person. And you do have to have a deep friendship because that's really what's going to sustain it way after the looks fade and things start to get ugly, no pun intended."
WORLD SERIES MVP, 'STAR WARS' ACTRESS SHARE HALLMARK-MOVIE LOVE STORY AFTER OVER 20 YEARS OF MARRIAGE

Hendrix said Lady Gaga and fiancé Michael Polansky are a "great example of two people who are living off-grid, living under the radar. And I don't know him, don't know her, but it does seem like that is the route you want to take versus, you know, going on social media with your guy and trying to help build him up."

title: Duncan Sheik, ‘Barely Breathing’ singer, dead at 56
summary: Duncan Sheik, the voice behind "Barely Breathing" and Tony-winning "Spring Awakening," died from organ failure at 56, his mother confirmed.
story: Singer-songwriter and Tony-winning composer Duncan Sheik speaks with Good Day New York in a 2001 interview about his work in music. Sheik died Sept. 17, 2026, at age 56.
Duncan Sheik, the singer-songwriter behind the hit "Barely Breathing" and the Tony and Grammy-winning musical "Spring Awakening," has died. He was 56.
Sheik died Thursday from organ failure, his mother, Suzanne Sheik, told The New York Times.
Representatives for Sheik did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOS
Duncan Sheik has died. The singer-songwriter was 56. (Gabriela Maj / Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)

"It is with profound sadness that we confirm the passing of Duncan Sheik. The world has a lost a singular talent, and deeply influential voice in music and theater," Sheik’s social media account posted Friday. "Duncan was a father, husband, son, brother, and friend. He will be remembered for his sensitivity, wit, intelligence, and depth of spirit he brought to those who knew and loved him."
The news comes after Sheik’s Instagram account shared an update on his health on Wednesday.

"Barely Breathing" singer Duncan Sheik, who later earned acclaim on Broadway for "Spring Awakening," died from organ failure at age 56, according to his mother. (Margaret Norton / NBCU Photo Bank / NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

"Duncan is currently receiving medical care and remains in critical but stable condition," the statement read. "Out of respect for Duncan and our family, we will not be sharing any further medical details at this time."
"We kindly ask for privacy during this incredibly difficult time and will provide updates when appropriate," the statement continued. "Thank you for the continued love and support."

The statement was released just before the Off-Broadway premiere of Sheik's new musical, "Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen," and coincided with the announcement of a new Off-Broadway staging of "Spring Awakening."
Duncan Sheik and Steven Sater accept an award for "Spring Awakening" on stage in 2007. (AP Photo/Jeff Christensen)
Throughout the summer of 2026, Sheik frequently posted photos of himself from the hospital on Instagram. He did not publicly share details about his condition.

His song "Barely Breathing," released in 1996, spent 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at No. 16. The song earned Sheik a Grammy nomination for best male pop vocal performance in 1998 and later found new audiences on shows including "Glee" and "Girls."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
While "Barely Breathing" made Sheik a familiar voice on ’90s radio, Broadway ultimately became a defining chapter of his career.
The "Spring Awakening" musical was adapted from a 19th-century play by German playwright Frank Wedekind, with music by Sheik and lyrics by playwright Steven Sater.

Lauren "Lolo" Pritchard, Steven Sater, Lea Michele, Jonathan Groff, Duncan Sheik and John Gallagher Jr. attend the premiere of "Spring Awakening: Those You’ve Known" in New York City in April 2022. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
"Spring Awakening" ran for 859 Broadway performances and won eight Tony Awards, including best musical, as well as a Grammy for best musical theater album.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
The original Broadway production helped launch the careers of actors including Jonathan Groff, Lea Michele, John Gallagher Jr. and Gideon Glick.

Sheik later brought his pop background to "American Psycho," which premiered in London before opening on Broadway in 2016. His other projects included "Whisper House," "Legerdemain" and the 2022 album "Claptrap."
Singer-songwriter Duncan Sheik earned a Grammy nomination for "Barely Breathing" before finding major success as a composer for musical theater. (Brian Ach/Invision/AP, File)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Born in Montclair, New Jersey, in 1969, Sheik split his childhood between New Jersey and South Carolina, picking up the guitar at a young age and getting his first synthesizer at 12.
Sheik is survived by his wife, Nora Ariffin, and their 7-year-old daughter, Ines.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Sydney Sweeney’s provocative sports ad 'reinforces the image she has already built' despite backlash: expert
summary: Sydney Sweeney's nude sports trading app ad drew backlash from Olympic athletes, but PR experts say it may not damage her brand at all.
story: Brand expert Adrienne Uthe explains that Sydney Sweeney's provocative ad has competing narratives, as expert says 'perception' can become 'reality.'
Sydney Sweeney sparked widespread backlash following the release of her provocative campaign for a sports trading app.
No stranger to controversy or criticism, Sweeney, 29, faced the music from Olympic athletes, entertainment icons and millions of keyboard warriors who voiced their opinions of the naked ad.

Adrienne Uthe, founder of Kronus Communications, exclusively told Fox News Digital that while Sweeney's latest ad may have ruffled feathers, "women having agency also means allowing women to make choices about their image that other women may not personally agree with."
SYDNEY SWEENEY FIRES BACK AT TROLLS AFTER FACING CRITICISM ONLINE FOR PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD
Sydney Sweeney posed in the nude for her latest campaign, a move that sparked controversy among athletes and experts. (TheStewartofNY)

"People are entitled to dislike the ad, just like women athletes are entitled to criticize it for their own reasons," Uthe said. "But I don't think this is materially damaging to Sydney Sweeney in any way, shape or form.

"In fact, I don't think it's a large departure from who she is and what her brand represents. She's a beautiful woman right now at the peak of her career, and she ultimately can decide which projects she wants to take and which ones she doesn't."
She added, "And she's chosen to make sexuality a part of her brand for better or for worse."
WATCH HERE: EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON SYDNEY SWEENEY PROVOCATIVE AD CONTROVERSY

Sweeney's latest ad featured several shots with strategically placed sports equipment covering her mostly nude body. "Think you know sports? Prove it. Novig is just sports. So, they wanted a show," the "Euphoria" star said in the campaign.
SYDNEY SWEENEY, SCOOTER BRAUN ROMANCE FACES BIGGEST CHALLENGE YET AS EXPERT WARNS COUPLE TO 'BE PREPARED'

Several female athletes didn’t appear to take too kindly to the ad. Australian Olympic gold medalist swimmer Ariarne Titmus, British sprinter Amy Hunt and former American gymnast Gracie Kramer were among those to denounce the ad.
Times Square billboards prominently showed off the provocative Sydney Sweeney ad.  (Anthony Behar/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)
Sydney Sweeney posed for the Novig sports trading app ad. (Getty Images)
Uthe believed Novig's creative team accomplished its goal, but stressed the significance of effective marketing.
"Going viral tells me they captured attention. It doesn’t tell me they captured the customer," Uthe said.

"This is where social media completely distorts reality, and we've seen this across all platforms in pop culture, politics, sports and beyond. So the narrative that is the loudest isn't necessarily what is true and what the majority opinion is."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Uthe noted that one side claimed the ad objectified women in sports, while the other narrative questions why there's outrage over an obviously provocative ad.
Sydney Sweeney faced the wrath of online critics after posing in a provocative new sports betting campaign. (Carlo Paloni)

"Once one of those frames takes over, whether it's through different content that someone is viewing or someone just inherently has a bias for this topic, that perception is really gonna make it a reality for them," Uthe said. "And that's why I always say, if you can make it trend, you can it true."
Olivia Bennett, senior account director at Go Up, thought that the campaign was simply "bad for women in sport."

"I can understand the commercial calculation behind choosing Sydney Sweeney," Bennett told Fox News Digital. "Novig will know its audience, and Sydney has built a public brand where sex appeal, provocation and controversy consistently generate attention.

title: Prince Harry, Meghan Markle feeding the 'publicity machine' despite privacy demands: expert
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle sources push back on King Charles's guidance labeling the Sussexes as private citizens, not royal representatives.
story: Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," argues Prince Harry and Meghan Markle choose publicity while seeking privacy and says their royal status should be made clear.
Sources close to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are "pushing back" after King Charles issued new guidance on the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's positions now that they are back in the United Kingdom.

King Charles issued guidance claiming that Harry and Markle are "akin to private citizens" via a letter issued by the Lord Chamberlain on Sept. 7. Sources told People magazine that Harry and Markle are "public figures" and that if Harry and Markle were private citizens, the Lord Chamberlain "would not have needed to issue a letter of formal guidance."
"Members of the public know who they are. The idea that they can live a normal, ‘private’ life is sadly not realistic," the source added.
King Charles issued a letter declaring Prince Harry and Meghan Markle private citizens after their return to the U.K. (Getty Images)

Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," addressed the "not realistic" claim by the source and told Fox News Digital that the "private citizen" guidance just means that they do not represent the king.
KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT

"I want to push back on this argument coming from People magazine and sources close to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle that it's somehow unrealistic for the Sussexes to live as private citizens. Being a private citizen does not mean you're anonymous. It simply means you don't represent the king. The jobs you accept and the responsibilities you take, you take them on as yourself, not the crown," Schofield began.
"In my opinion, you can't repeatedly feed the publicity machine and then complain about a lack of privacy."

Schofield drew a comparison between Princess Anne's children – Zara Tindall and Peter Phillips. Princess Anne is Queen Elizabeth's only daughter and the sister of King Charles. She chose not to give her two kids royal titles at birth.

"They're recognizable, have commercial interests, attend major royal family events, but they do not represent the monarch, yet they have both successfully built lives outside of the working institution. Harry and Meghan could pursue a quieter life, a life like Zara and Peter. They choose not to. In my opinion, you can't repeatedly feed the publicity machine and then complain about a lack of privacy," she said.
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE CAN'T HAVE PUBLICITY AND PRIVACY: EXPERT
Schofield argued that the king’s clarification was necessary as Harry and Markle’s public profile has become increasingly intertwined with the controversies surrounding them.
MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK RETURN POSES PALACE CONTROL ‘NIGHTMARE,’ EXPERT WARNS

"Prince Harry is classified as a non-working member of the royal family whose position is akin to a private citizen. Of course, Harry and Meghan are famous. Nobody's disputing that, but where does their fame end and infamy begin? Fame can inspire people to invest in you emotionally and financially. Infamy means people know your name because controversy follows you," she began.
Meghan Markle, Prince Harry and King Charles in 2018. (Getty Images)

Schofield continued, "And after years of feuds, lawsuits and relationships that deteriorate, I think it's fair to ask how much of the Sussex's enormous public profile today is driven by admiration and how much is driven by controversy, which is precisely why the king has every reason to make their status crystal clear."
Ian Pelham Turner, royal broadcaster, disagrees with Charles's stance on labeling his son and his wife as private citizens.

"Harry is the son of a king. He has prominence in Britain. Thus, whether William likes it or not the king should decide not to weakly disenfranchise his second son," Turner said. "He is a billionaire with vast fortunes. Pay for his son’s full security rather than looking like an Ebenezer Scrooge after."
Sources close to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle told People that they are having security concerns. (WireImage/Getty Images)

He continued, "Although some royals still live in Dickens times, we are actually in the 21st century. How would the king feel if a second tragedy happens in his lifetime, first Diana, and potentially Harry and his family?"
Private citizens are not granted security like members of the royal family are.
Richard Fitzwilliams, royal commentator, told Fox News Digital that Charles' letter, declaring Harry and Markle private citizens, is a "total mess."

"The current situation with the king’s letter about their status and the Sussexes' response is a total mess. The raising of the security issue which, in the Sussexes' view, is a further example of the risks they face, was, in fact, highlighting the incompetence on their part as no proper recce [reconnaissance] has been done during term by their team," Fitzwilliams said.
Prince Harry is King Charles' second son. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
Fitzwilliams argued that the king's letter was a "slap on the wrist" for Meghan and Harry, proving his lack of trust for the former senior royals.

"The king’s letter restated the facts without giving them much of a chance to 'clarify' things. It was clearly intended as a slap on the wrist and evidence that the king didn’t trust them. Unfortunately, nothing is going to stop matters becoming a circus, with royal engagements overshadowed by what they get up to," he said.
As for what's to come, the royal experts are stumped.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle returned to the U.K. six years after leaving for California. (Getty Images)

"It is simply impossible to anticipate the way this may go. It is only clear that, whatever their motives and mistakes, the Sussexes are news whatever they do. That strengthens their hand because it gives them a very high profile. This has nothing to do with the rights and wrongs of any issues involved," Fitzwilliams said.
Schofield explained that Markle and Harry are "unpredictable."

"Harry and Meghan are unpredictable. The palace can't have governments, charities, businesses, even members of the public wondering whether their activities somehow carry the endorsement of the crown. It doesn't. They don't. King Charles is saying, absolutely not," she said.

Since marrying in 2018 and making their royal exit in 2020, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex have been attempting to carve out their own independent roles outside the monarchy. (Joshua Sammer/Getty Images)

Schofield continued, "Harry spent years insisting that he wanted independence from the institution. Independence means you don't get to demand the privileges or the authority or the special treatment afforded to people who stayed and did the job. It's the king who determines who represents the crown, not Prince Harry, not Meghan Markle, and certainly not anonymous sources briefing People Magazine. Harry wanted his freedom from the system. title: Ed Sheeran faces growing backlash as radio station bans songs, protest groups respond to Macklemore's removal
summary: Classic Hits Radio announced it will stop playing Ed Sheeran's music after backlash over Macklemore's removal from the Loop Tour over Gaza protests.
story: Fox News host Sean Hannity discusses rapper Macklemore being removed from Ed Sheeran's tour over the rapper's 'Free Palestine' stance, weighing the backlash, the broader debate over free speech and public accountability and how the controversy has sparked renewed discussion about celebrities' political activism on 'Hannity.'
Ed Sheeran continues to deal with the backlash surrounding Macklemore's removal from the singer’s U.S. tour.

An Irish radio station announced Thursday that, in response to the controversy and feedback from listeners, it would no longer play music released by the 35-year-old "Shape of You" singer for the "foreseeable future."

Dave Kelly, group program director at Bay Broadcasting, which runs Classic Hits Radio, told The Independent the decision "has been carefully considered" and "is not intended as a personal judgment on Ed Sheeran."

"We acknowledge his own explanation of the circumstances surrounding recent events," Kelly said. "As an independent Irish-owned radio station, however, we believe it is important to listen to our audience and to stand alongside Irish artists who have made what is undoubtedly a significant professional decision based on their own convictions."
An Irish radio station announced it will not be playing Sheeran's music for the "foreseeable future." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for iHeartRadio)
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO
He added his company "believe(s) in peace, humanity and respect" as well as "the right of people and artists to express and act upon their sincerely held views."

"In light of the strength of feeling expressed by our listeners and the decisions taken by Irish artists involved in the tour, we believe removing Ed Sheeran’s music from our playlist is the appropriate decision for Classic Hits Radio at this time," he concluded.

The controversy began after Macklemore repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song, "Hind’s Hall," during his opening performance at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, Sept. 4 and 5.
Advertisement

He was then dropped as an opening act on Sheeran's Loop Tour. The "Thrift Shop" singer alleged that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft pressured Sheeran into dropping him from the tour, telling the singer he would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium and by encouraging other stadium owners to issue a similar ultimatum.
Macklemore was kicked off Ed Sheeran's stadium tour over his "Free Palestine" remarks. (Getty Images)
Following Macklemore's removal from the tour, four other supporting acts chose to drop out, including Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, Lukas Graham and Finneas.

In addition to the radio station's decision to temporarily remove his music from its catalog, the pro-Palestine groups Philly Palestine Coalition and Shut Down D&Z have planned a protest outside of Sheeran's Philadelphia concert.

They shared a flyer on Instagram urging people to attend the protest on Sept. 19 outside Lincoln Financial Field. The flier reads, "Gaza is our compass" and "Billionaires, Zionists & Warmongers out of Philly."

"Palestine returns to headlines across the world and we return to the streets to fight for Gaza. Free Palestine is not a tagline for celebrities or a slogan for online statements," they wrote in the caption.

"A free Palestine is the work of generations of Palestinian resistance, a free Palestine is the compass for all oppressed people, a free Palestine demands nothing less than total liberation. Free Palestine is a call to direct action. On Saturday, we take to the streets to return the conversation to Palestine, and return Philadelphia to action."
Pro-Palestine groups have planned protests at Sheeran's concert in Philadelphia. (Earl Gibson III/Deadline via Getty Images)
They continued, writing that Sheeran removed Macklemore from his tour "in the name of 'neutrality' and being 'apolitical' and due to threats from stadium owners, including Lincoln Financial Field."
"There is no neutrality against oppression, only complicity. When the news cycle has moved on, we will still be here. Join us. FREE PALESTINE, FREE LEBANON, FREE CUBA, FREE CONGO, FREE SUDAN."

Sheeran addressed the controversy on Instagram, writing, "I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care.

"After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote. "I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said.

"I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final."
Ed Sheeran responded to Macklemore's claims over tour removal. (Getty Images)

He added that the decision to remove Macklemore from the tour was the promoter's and that "Macklemore’s contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me."

"There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he added. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace.

"I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change."

"Here's the thing is that I told the people – that said that I was lying – back then," she added. "They already knew. But I got this letter."

MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SAYS SHE AND VALERIE BERTINELLI DRANK WINE, DID COCAINE DURING SITCOM BREAKS

Alan Ritchson is sharing an intensely personal account of a period when he says his life began to unravel.

The "Reacher" star said a former business partner threatened to accuse him of rape if he refused to meet her at a hotel in Cannes, France – an alleged threat he says left him overwhelmed by uncertainty and depression.
"I'm a suicide survivor," he said during a recent appearance at FAN EXPO Canada.

"I lost everything in that relationship; she was a billionaire, and she actually tanked every bit of our business and cost me a lot, and also the threat of that looming over my head – I hired a litigator to fight back and make sure that couldn't happen," Ritchson said.

"I ended up winning a settlement, but I didn't win anything because what I was left with was this uncertainty about what happens in life when you do good, you know, and like when you try your hardest."

title: 'American Idol' ditches Hollywood for Georgia after two decades as California loses another production
summary: "American Idol" is relocating from Hollywood to an Atlanta-area studio complex as Georgia's tax incentives and infrastructure lure major productions.
story: California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton joins ‘America’s Newsroom’ to discuss President Donald Trump’s push for a federal film tax credit to bring entertainment jobs back to California. He also weighs in on a new state tire regulation and a Los Angeles crosswalk controversy.
"American Idol" is ditching Hollywood for Georgia amid renewed concerns about California’s competitiveness.

On Wednesday, Fremantle, the production company behind ABC's long-running singing competition, confirmed the relocation to Fox News Digital. The company is reportedly in final discussions with an Atlanta-area studio complex, according to Deadline.
Longtime fans and viewers of the show were quick to react on social media.
"'You’re going to…Atlanta!' Just doesn’t have that same ring to it," one user wrote on X.
"Another one bites the dust LA. Sad!" another added.
"So much for those 'hollyweird' tax breaks eh?" one person quipped.
NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE'
Lionel Richie, Carrie Underwood, Ryan Seacrest and Luke Bryan will be filming the 27th season of "American Idol" in Georgia. (Disney via Getty Images)
"LOL !!! Another production Hollywood GETTING THE HELL OUT OF CALIFORNIA ! AFTER 25 YEARS BYEEEEE GAVIN NEWSOM American Idol is OUT OF CALI," another wrote.

While the move marks a significant change for a series long associated with Hollywood, Lisa Cusack, president of the Don’t L.A. My Burbank PAC, said the relocation should be a warning to California officials.

"The issue is that Georgia offers generous incentives for reality TV shows, while California often leaves them behind," Cusack told Fox News Digital. "For example, Nick Schultz’s entertainment tax credit bill, AB 2319, specifically excludes unscripted programming."

"Now Georgia has a lot of the same infrastructure as Hollywood, and offers a less expensive, more family-friendly quality of life," she continued. "There’s very little keeping even Hollywood business in California anymore. This should serve as a five-shot-espresso wake-up call to Rob Bonta to settle with Paramount and not make things worse."

Last month, Paramount CEO David Ellison threatened to relocate the company’s headquarters to a more business-friendly state such as Georgia, Tennessee or Texas if California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading 11 other states in an effort to block Paramount's $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), did not negotiate a settlement by Oct. 1.

The next season of "Idol" will premiere next year. (Eric McCandless/Disney via Getty Images)

As Puck News reported, Ellison could move Paramount — and potentially Warner Bros. Discovery if he ultimately merges the companies — out of California "regardless of the eventual outcome of the case." Ellison has even developed a five-year plan that would relocate the vast majority of jobs out of the state while still maintaining a footprint in Hollywood.

On Wednesday, TMZ reported that the Los Angeles Mayor's Office and the California Attorney General's Office were told Paramount would announce Tuesday that it was leaving California. No such announcement had been made as of Wednesday.

"I tried to warn you," Spencer Pratt wrote on X following the TMZ news. "LA is getting absolutely decimated by the insane communist wackos running California. Bob Bonta’s jihad against Paramount is a death blow. What a corrupt piece of s---."

According to Deadline, Georgia has become one of the country’s most competitive production hubs by offering a 20% base film and television tax credit, with a potential 10% promotional uplift for qualifying projects. The state’s official guidelines list television series among eligible productions and require at least $500,000 in qualified Georgia spending.
Stephen Weizenecker, a partner at Barnes & Thornburg in Georgia, said there are three pillars to analyze when deciding whether to film in California or Georgia.

"Physical infrastructure is equally critical. A show like 'American Idol' requires massive sound stages, specialized equipment for elaborate performance sets, live-audience capacity, and proximity to rehearsal spaces, wardrobe, and production offices," said Weizenecker, who has had a direct role in developing Georgia's entertainment tax incentive framework and spent over two decades advising productions on filming all across the world.
"Idol" judge Carrie Underwood is one of many celebrities who has fled Los Angeles. (Christopher Willard/Disney via Getty Images)

"Georgia now offers purpose-built studio campuses — including Tyler Perry Studios, Trilith Studios and Assembly Studios — that rival Los Angeles market in scale and amenities. I have worked closely with many of these facilities as they grew from concept to world-class campuses, and I can attest to their capacity to support the most demanding productions."
Weizenecker said production tax incentives often serve as the "decisive tipping point" once the infrastructure boxes are checked.

"As someone instrumental in crafting the Georgia Entertainment Industry Investment Act, I have seen firsthand how Georgia's program offers structural advantages over California's that make it exceptionally attractive for a recurring, high-budget unscripted series."
Additionally, Georgia has invested strategically in workforce development since the enactment of the Georgia Entertainment Industry Investment Act, according to Weizenecker.

"The Georgia Film Academy, a collaboration among the University System of Georgia, the Technical College System of Georgia and the Georgia Department of Economic Development, has trained thousands of professionals across disciplines from grip and electric to visual effects. That pipeline, reinforced by the sheer volume of annual production activity, has created a self-sustaining ecosystem of IATSE-qualified crew members who live and work in the state full-time."

Discovery (WBD), did not negotiate a settlement by Oct. 1. (Michael Yanow/NurPhoto via Getty Images; Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)

"Virtually every major production services vendor — equipment rental, transportation, catering, construction and specialty providers — now maintains a permanent Georgia presence," he continued. "Post-production facilities offering editorial, color grading, sound mixing and VFX have expanded significantly, with several national and international post houses establishing Atlanta-area operations."

"The same infrastructure supporting Marvel, Lucasfilm, Netflix and major network television productions is available to a show of 'American Idol's' caliber," he added. "Having advised many of the productions and facilities that anchor this ecosystem, I can confirm Georgia's vendor community is fully capable of supporting this show."
The show’s relocation also underscores how its talent is already less tied to Los Angeles.
Carrie Underwood, who won "American Idol" in 2005 and now serves as one of the show’s judges, has lived with her family on a 400-acre farm in Franklin, Tennessee, since leaving Hollywood in 2019.

Underwood has described her Tennessee home as the place where she and her husband, former NHL player Mike Fisher, raise their two sons, care for livestock and grow vegetables.
In a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Underwood said farm life is the opposite of her on-camera career and that she takes pride in being a hands-on mother when she is home.

title: Macklemore donates $1M to Palestinian aid organizations after Ed Sheeran tour fallout
summary: Macklemore is donating $1 million from Ed Sheeran's U.S. "Loop Tour" to Palestinian aid groups and challenged Robert Kraft to match his contribution.
story: Rapper Macklemore causes chaos on Ed Sheerans tour after making anti-Israel comments at a concert. Ed Sheeran responds to the backlash, explaining that the decision to remove Macklemore was made by promoters.

Macklemore announced that he is donating the $1 million he earned opening for Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour to organizations providing humanitarian aid to Palestinians, prompting a public response from New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft.

On Monday, the 43-year-old rapper was dropped from Sheeran's "Loop Tour" after he repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" during his opening act at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4 and 5.

Macklemore alleged that Kraft, 85, pressured Sheeran to remove him from the tour by telling the singer he would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium and by rallying other stadium owners to issue a similar ultimatum. Kraft later confirmed he opposed Macklemore's participation at Gillette based on what he described as the "Thrift Shop" rapper's history of antisemitic rhetoric.
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO
Sheeran, 35, has said the decision was made by the tour promoter and venue owners, not by him personally.

In an Instagram post on Wednesday, Macklemore shared his plans to donate his paycheck from the "Loop Tour" to six organizations, including the Palestine Children's Relief Fund (PCRF), HEAL Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, UNRWA USA National Committee and American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA).

"With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom," he wrote.
Macklemore announced that he is donating $1 million in earnings from Ed Sheeran's tour after he was dropped. (Redferns)

"I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people," he continued. "And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth."

"I want to center the parents carrying their children into hospitals without the basic resources to treat them, and the physicians, paramedics, journalists and aid workers who keep going back in. I want to center the organizers and activists who have paid real costs for standing with Palestine," Macklemore added. "Their risk is of a far different order than mine."
HANNAH EINBINDER'S BRUTAL MESSAGE TO ED SHEERAN FUELS GROWING CELEBRITY REVOLT OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR DRAMA
Macklemore noted that "writing a check is one of the least costly forms of solidarity to me."
"I am doing it because I can and because these organizations are doing the work while much of the world debates it," he wrote.

"Palestinians have lived for decades without basic rights and should not have to wait another day to be free," Macklemore added. "That is where my focus will remain. I will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and their fight for liberation."
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE
"When the news cycle moves on, which it will, don’t move with it," he concluded. "Free Palestine."

Shortly after the rapper challenged Kraft to match his contribution, Kraft said Sheeran had already asked him to commit $2 million to match the singer's own donation toward humanitarian relief in the region.
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said Sheeran asked to match his $2M contribution to humanitarian aid in the region. (Ron Chenoy/Imagn Images)

"I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people. I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting. Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region and fight this humanitarian crisis," Kraft wrote in a statement shared on Gillette Stadium's social media pages.
MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS
"Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges," Kraft continued.

"In addition, I’d like the people who are speaking in support of the Palestinian people to know that for decades, I have supported efforts that create opportunity for Palestinians and have brought young Palestinians and Israelis together to build businesses, create jobs, and forge relationships," he added.

title: King Charles responds to Charles Spencer's claims about Princess Diana in a rare statement
summary: King Charles broke royal protocol with a rare palace statement responding to Charles Spencer's explosive claims in his upcoming memoir, "Swan Song."
story: A reported movie about Princess Diana spearheaded by Prince Harry for the 30th anniversary of her death is causing royal family tension. Johnny Joey Jones reacts with a theory about Markle acting as an American plant to dismantle the monarchy, sparking laughs from the co-hosts.
King Charles responded to claims made about him in Charles Spencer's upcoming book in an unusual move.

The Daily Mail published an excerpt of Spencer's upcoming memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Wednesday, in which the king's former brother-in-law alleged a heated conversation he had with Charles after the death of his sister and the former Princess of Wales, Princess Diana.

"Prince Charles continued his stream of anger, without me interrupting. Then he stopped. I assumed the pause signaled an effort to bring himself under control, but then he unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death," Spencer alleged, according to the Daily Mail. "‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’"

According to the excerpt, the disagreement between King Charles and the 9th Earl of Spencer was regarding the decision to have Prince William and Prince Harry, then 15 and 12, walk behind their mother's casket during the funeral procession.
King Charles responds to claims made by Charles Spencer in his new memoir. (Getty Images)
KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare statement on behalf of the king responding to Spencer's claims.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said, according to People.

Princess Diana died in August 1997 at age 36 after suffering injuries sustained in a car accident in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, France. Her partner, Dodi Fayed, and the driver, Henri Paul, also died in the crash.

The first winner of "The Voice of Holland," Ben Saunders, was found dead at the age of 43.
According to local newspaper De Telegraaf, Saunders was found at the popular recreational lake, Rijkerswoerdse Plassen, in the Netherlands, on Tuesday, Sept. 15.
Police recovered his body from the lake at 1:20 p.m. local time, DutchNews reported. No cause of death has been revealed.

"We can confirm that a body was found yesterday at a recreational lake of Arnhem and that police have ruled out foul play," the Police Unit East Netherlands told People magazine. "We do not release or comment on personal details."

Ben had a beautiful beautiful family and a family that loves him very much and always will… Ben is in my heart and he will stay there forever ❤️🙏"

title: Kelly Osbourne draws a line with estranged sister Aimee: 'I don't want you in my life'
summary: Kelly Osbourne says she resents never having a big sister and claims Aimee Osbourne seemed "embarrassed" of the family during their reality show era.
story: (Video credit: AP via SKY) Sharon, Jack, Aimee, Louis and Kelly Osbourne paid their respects to Ozzy Osbourne at his funeral in Birmingham.
Kelly Osbourne reflected on the lost relationship with her estranged older sister, Aimee Osbourne.

The youngest daughter of late rock legend Ozzy Osbourne admitted on an episode of the "We Need To Talk" podcast that she's not close with her sister, but that she did "respect her enough to, you know, keep her anonymity."

"I believe there's a reason for everything; it just wasn't meant to be for her," she explained of Aimee's decision against participating in the family's wildly successful reality show, "The Osbournes."
KELLY OSBOURNE SAYS SHE 'WASN'T WELL' WHILE FACING HARSH SCRUTINY, BODY-SHAMING AFTER DAD OZZY'S DEATH
Kelly Osbourne admitted there was no hope for reconciliation with her estranged older sister, Aimee Osbourne. (Dave Benett)
"It was always me and Jack," she said. "If I'm honest, my older sister didn't really ever acknowledge me and my brother. She was just in her own world doing her own thing.
"And I do, to a certain extent, if I'm honest, feel as though she was embarrassed of us... the whole family."
JACK OSBOURNE TELLS CRITICS TO 'SHUT THE F--- UP' AFTER BACKLASH OVER WHITE HOUSE UFC FIGHT ATTENDANCE
The Osbournes became a household name in the early 2000s when MTV shone a light into their lives as celebrities — and the children of rock royalty — with an unscripted show about the family.
The Osbourne family starred in their own reality show in the 2000s. (Dave Hogan)

The Prince of Darkness earned legions of new fans from the show, which also featured wife Sharon, and two of their three kids: Jack and Kelly. Aimee, who lived in the guest house at the time, opted out of appearing on the program.
The series premiered in 2002 and ran for four seasons, with a final curtain call in 2005.

Kelly said there was no hope for a reconciliation.

title: Hannah Einbinder's brutal message to Ed Sheeran fuels growing celebrity revolt over Macklemore tour drama
summary: Hannah Einbinder roasted Ed Sheeran on Instagram after Macklemore was dropped from the "Loop Tour" over his onstage pro-Palestinian comments.
story: 'The Gun Show' host Mike 'Gunz' Gunzelman discusses four opening acts quitting Ed Sheeran's concert tour after Macklemore was dropped. Gunzelman analyzes online pressure on performers to take political positions and compares the music industry reaction to 2024 college campus demonstrations.
Hannah Einbinder has taken aim at Ed Sheeran amid the growing backlash over Macklemore’s removal from the singer’s U.S. tour.
The "Hacks" star criticized Sheeran on Instagram, joking that she was speaking "as a ginger" before wishing him an especially painful sunburn.
"Ed Sheeran i say this as a ginger. i hope you get a REALLY bad sun burn the kind on the back of your entire body where it hurts to lie down or walk or sit," Einbinder wrote.
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTIAN STANCE
Hannah Einbinder slammed Ed Sheeran over his Palestinian stance. (Getty Images)
Her post came after Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran’s Loop Tour after onstage comments supporting Palestinians.
Einbinder was among several celebrities to publicly call out Sheeran, who addressed the controversy in a lengthy statement posted Tuesday.

"Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist," Sheeran wrote on social media. "As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing."

On Monday, Macklemore had claimed that Sheeran told him Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had rallied other stadium owners to oppose allowing the rapper to perform. According to his account, the venues allegedly gave Sheeran an ultimatum: "If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

Sheeran’s statement offered a different account of the events, saying that, after Macklemore’s performances at his New Jersey shows, venues scheduled for upcoming tour dates told organizers they would pull the shows if Macklemore remained on the lineup.
"After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote.

"I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Macklemore was kicked off Sheeran's tour due to his pro-Palestinian remarks.  (Kevin Mazur/WireImage)

Sheeran said he has deliberately avoided using his professional platform for politics because his audience includes young people and children from diverse backgrounds. Sheeran said concertgoers attend his shows expecting "a place of safety and sanctuary" rather than a political forum.

"There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he wrote. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace.

"I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change."
Sheeran also rejected the suggestion that his decision not to speak publicly about his personal beliefs made him indifferent to the conflict.

"I am not complicit," he wrote. "I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care."
MICK JAGGER DOESN'T WANT TO 'LECTURE' FANS, SAYS HIS JOB IS TO MAKE PEOPLE 'HAVE THE BEST TIME'
However, his statement has done little to quiet the criticism.

"Wicked" actor Marissa Bode accused Sheeran of lacking a backbone, writing that although she uses a wheelchair, she still has a "f---ing spine," before adding her support for Palestinians on Instagram.
"Ed Sheeran, my legs may not work like they used to before, but at least I have a f---ing spine. Free Palestine, b----," she wrote.
Marissa Bode slammed Sheeran, calling him a "b----." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images)
Children’s educator and YouTube sensation Ms. Rachel similarly said Sheeran had "caved" to people who opposed Macklemore’s advocacy and argued that silence over Gaza is not neutral.

"Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won’t be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine. Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it."

Ms. Rachel, also known as Rachel Griffin-Accurso, has been open about her stance throughout the years.  (Variety via Getty Images)
PAUL MCCARTNEY SAYS BEATLES CLASSIC UNITES AUDIENCES 'IN TRUMP’S AMERICA' DESPITE POLITICAL DIVIDE

Former Pink Floyd member Roger Waters delivered one of the harshest responses, posting a video in which he contrasted Macklemore’s willingness to speak out with Sheeran’s refusal to take a public position.

"I just have a little message for you," he said in a video he shared on social media. "There are two kinds of people in this world, Ed. There are people who do the right thing. That rapper Macklemore would be one of those people. And there are people, many of them sadly little – excuse me, I nearly used the F-word then, p------ like you who do the wrong thing. Goodbye."
Macklemore has also criticized Sheeran’s stance, though he said their friendship was not necessarily over.

He argued that Sheeran could not move beyond his public position of "not taking sides," adding that refusing to choose a side in an unequal conflict does not amount to neutrality.
The fallout has also affected Sheeran’s touring lineup.
Responding to Macklemore's claims, Sheeran said he was "not complicit."  (Dia Dipasupil)
Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Irish folk band Beoga all announced that they would withdraw from upcoming dates in solidarity with Macklemore.
Finneas said artists should not be silenced when speaking for oppressed people, while Rowe condemned the use of wealth and venue power to suppress pro-Palestinian voices.
Lukas Graham wrote that he was grateful for his friendship with Sheeran but couldn't "carry on with tour as things stand" before withdrawing.
"I'm sorry we won't be there. This is a difficult decision, but it's one I need to stand by," Graham added.
Macklemore has been speaking about Palestinians for three years and said now is not the time to be silenced.  (Fox News Digital)

A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's tour.

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement to Rolling Stone.
"After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."
While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he stands by his position.

"I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. I needed 2. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine. But if those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on."

title: Jelly Roll says he could walk away from country music if God tells him to: ‘Y’all will never see me again’
summary: After three Grammys, a Grand Ole Opry membership and his divorce from Bunnie Xo, Jelly Roll says he may walk away from country music for good.
story: Jelly Roll tells Fox News Digital what it means to him to celebrate the 60th Academy of Country Music Awards.
Jelly Roll isn't ruling out walking away from country music altogether.
The Grammy-winning singer revealed that if God calls him to a different purpose, he could leave the music business behind — and fans might never see him again.

The "Son of a Sinner" singer made the candid admission in a previously recorded interview with "Y’all Access Radio’s" Kelly Sutton while backstage at the Grand Ole Opry in March. The interview was published on Sept. 13.
POST MALONE ABRUPTLY CANCELS UPCOMING TOUR DATES WITH JELLY ROLL: ‘WE AIN’T READY’
Jelly Roll has said he is considering what comes next in his career after reaching major milestones in country music. (Matt Jelonek/Getty Images)

"Everything that Jason or Jelly Roll wanted to do in the music business, I’ve done now, so at this point, I really need to go talk to God and see if he wants me to stick around, or what he wants me to do next," Jelly Roll, whose real name is Jason DeFord, said.

"If God tells me to go work at a homeless shelter in Paducah, Ky., I’m outta here, you know what I'm saying? Y’all will never see me again, and I’ll be working at a… he gave me everything I ever wanted, man — Grammys, ACMs, CMAs, I’m a member of the Grand Ole Opry, like God has done it."
JELLY ROLL SAYS HE 'LOST HIS WAY' AFTER SHEDDING OVER 200 POUNDS, REVEALS HOW MUCH WEIGHT HE GAINED BACK
Jelly Roll accepts the award for best contemporary country album for "Beautifully Broken" on stage during the 68th Annual Grammy Awards. (Valerie Macon/AFP via Getty Images)
Jelly Roll said he has already checked off virtually every box on his music career list.
The Nashville star has gone from a troubled past to becoming one of country music's biggest stars, with hits including "Son of a Sinner" and "Need a Favor."
But now he says he's trying to figure out whether music is still where he's supposed to be.

"I just got to go do a little bit of work on myself to make sure that I’m all the way ready," Jelly Roll said. "I’m completely sober, though. I’m clear-headed, and I’m deep in therapy, I’m deep in my Bible, but I think that I got to separate from the chaos of the business for me to really hear what God wants to do for me next."
Guest host Jelly Roll appears on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" on Aug. 26. (Disney via Getty Images)
The comments follow an eventful year for the country star, including changes in his personal life and major career milestones.
Jelly Roll also drew political backlash this summer after guest-hosting "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and taking aim at President Donald Trump's weight, physical fitness and approval ratings.

"Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you'll be happy to see your p---- again," he joked.

The singer later pushed back on suggestions that he had suddenly become a liberal voice. "Sure, I lean left on some things," he said. "But like most folks, I’m pretty down the middle. I am a Christian. I am a country music singer. I’m a farmer. I’m a bow hunter."
Jelly Roll and Bunnie Xo married in 2016 and finalized their divorce in July 2026. (Taylor Hill/Getty Images)

After nearly a decade of marriage, their divorce was finalized in July.

title: Macklemore's long history of controversy from Grammy wins to 'Free Palestine' concert remarks
summary: Macklemore's pro-Palestinian concert remarks and controversial moments long predate his removal from Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour" over his "Hind's Hall" performance.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Macklemore's activism began long before his pro-Palestinian plight during Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour."
The musician, who's full name is Ben Haggerty, was kicked off Sheeran's tour following backlash from his "Free Palestine" messaging during his opening act at MetLife Stadium over the weekend.
While the fallout continues now that four supporting acts have withdrawn from the tour, Macklemore, 43, is no stranger to controversy and has often used his platform to amplify political issues.
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO 'BUILD A BRIDGE' OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO
Macklemore has a long history of using his public platform to amplify activism. (Arnaud Finistre)
The artist broke into the mainstream music scene in 2012 with the release of "The Heist," his debut studio album as the duo Macklemore & Ryan Lewis.

He faced criticism for sweeping the 2014 Grammys with four awards, which included winning the Best Rap Album Grammy over fan favorite Kendrick Lamar, who was equally nominated for seven awards that night.
MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE
Macklemore reached out to Lamar after the show and shared a screenshot of his text on social media where he told the "Humble" rapper that he was "robbed" of the win.

"My text to Kendrick after the show. He deserved best rap album... I'm honored and completely blown away to win anything much less 4 Grammys," Macklemore wrote. "But in that category, he should have won IMO. And that's taking nothing away from The Heist. Just giving GKMC it's proper respect."
More than 30 couples married during a Macklemore & Ryan Lewis performance of "Same Love" at the 2014 Grammy Awards. (Robert Gauthier)
Macklemore & Ryan Lewis sang with Madonna at the 2014 Grammy Awards where Queen Latifah presided over dozens of same-sex and heterosexual weddings during the performance. (Cliff Lipson)

He added, "With that being said, thank you to the fans. You're the reason we were on that stage tonight. And to play Same Love on that platform was a career highlight. The greatest honor of all. That's what this is about. Progress and art. Thank you."

Grammy viewers witnessed Macklemore & Ryan Lewis perform "Same Love" on stage to a mass wedding between 33 same-sex and heterosexual couples, officiated by Queen Latifah. At the end of the performance, Madonna appeared on stage for a rendition of her song, "Open Your Heart."
BLACK CROWES FACE BACKLASH AFTER CHRIS ROBINSON SHUTS DOWN U.S.A. CHANT AND CALLS FANS 'IGNORANT'

That same year, Macklemore faced backlash following an appearance with Ryan Lewis at The Museum of Pop Culture in Seattle, where he wore a black wig, beard and fake nose, which some claimed was an antisemitic costume.
The singer issued an apology shortly after and said that his costume wasn't intended to reflect a caricature of a Jewish man, but that he was trying to disguise himself in the crowd.
Macklemore issued an apology in 2014 after appearing in what critics called an antisemitic costume at an event in Seattle. (Suzi Pratt)

"Family, friends and fans alike who know me well, know that I'm absolutely not the person described in certain headlines today," he wrote on his website. "There is no worse feeling than being misunderstood, especially when people are hurt or offended."

"I respect all cultures and all people," he continued. "I would never intentionally put down anybody for the fabric that makes them who they are. I love human beings, love originality, and ... happen to love a weird outfit from time to time."
He also posted on X, "A fake witches nose, wig, and beard = random costume. Not my idea of a stereotype of anybody."

In 2023, he was one of many who signed the Arists4Ceasefire letter in support of Palestinian rights and humanitarian aid for Gaza and the following year released "Hind's Hall," an anthem supporting pro-Palestinian student protestors.
During a performance at Seattle's Palestine Will Live Forever festival, Macklemore faced heavy criticism after leading an anti-U.S. chant where he encouraged the crowd to say, "F- - - America."
Macklemore was one of many who signed the Arists4Ceasefire letter in support of Palestinian rights and humanitarian aid for Gaza. (Kieran Frost/Redferns)

"My thoughts and feelings are not always expressed perfectly or politely," he said on social media at the time. "Sometimes I slip up and get caught in the moment. Saturday night was one of those times.
PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS
He added, "Unfortunately, the historic event in my hometown that brought thousands of people together to raise awareness and money for the people of Palestine has become overshadowed by two words."
Macklemore admitted that he "lost endorsements, I've lost shows, I've lost business ties," but that his support remained "unwavering."
Macklemore said his "thoughts and feelings are not always expressed perfectly or politely," following backlash from an anti-American chant. (Isaac Brekken)
