title: Margaret Cho Tells Craig 1 Gesture From a ‘Golden Girls’ Star Made Her Think ‘I’m Going to Be OK’ in Hollywood
summary: Margaret Cho recalls Rue McClanahan helping calm her down during her first TV series role when she appeared on the ‘Golden Girls” spinoff, “The Golden Palace.”
story: Margaret Cho has cemented herself as a comedy icon, but she had some help when she first started out.

While appearing on the Sept. 15 episode of Craig Melvin’s “Glass Half Full” video podcast, Cho, who starred in the sitcom “All-American Girl” and earned an Emmy nomination for her guest turn on “30 Rock,” says another legendary star helped set her on the path where she knew she could make it in show business.
Craig asked if there was a moment that helped mold Cho into the person fans know today.
“It was one moment ... one of my very, very first television jobs. I was on a show called ‘Golden Palace,’ which was the spin-off of ‘Golden Girls,’” she said.

“So I had a part where my character — this is of course, very long time ago — so they had sort of like written a part for me where I didn’t speak English, and the only time I spoke English was when I sang. I sang ‘Moon River,’” she added.
Cho said she was nervous, but one of the show’s stars, Rue McClanahan, came to her aid.
“I was so scared to sing it and Rue McClanahan positioned herself — she actually volunteered this,” Cho recalled.

“She could tell that I was scared, and she put her hand on my back and she said, ‘OK, I’m going to count you in and I’m going to hum the key, so that you don’t do it off-key, so you can hear it in your ear, and then you can start the song,’” she said.
Cho was in awe of McClanahan, who died in 2010, taking a moment to help her out.

“It was such a generous act of, ‘I see you’re a scared kid, and I’m going to give you some confidence. I can’t sing the song for you, but I can start this off for you,’” she said. “She tapped in right before I start and then hummed the perfect note, because she’s also a singer — has perfect pitch — right in my ear, and I got it right.”
Cho appeared in one 1992 episode of “The Golden Palace,” which aired for only one season. It marked her second onscreen credit and first TV series. The experience left quite an impression on Cho.

“Hollywood is so scary. I’m this young person, going out here. I’m not white. I’m not a beauty. I’m not any of these things that you’re supposed to be in Hollywood, but I think I’m going to be OK,” she recalled.
Having such a big star take interest in her and help her made her realize “people are going to take care of me out here, and that actually turned out to be true,” she said.
Cho also cited Jerry Seinfeld, Rosie O’Donnell and Bob Hope as some of the other big names who helped her in her career.
“(They were) people who really took an interest and gave me jobs and helped me get into the place that I am in now, nearly four decades later,” she said.

title: Who Is Lizzie Borden, the Subject Of Netflix’s ‘Monster’ Season 4?
summary: Experts weigh in on the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden and their accused killer, Lizzie Borden, who is the subject of Netflix’s new season of “Monster”
story: On Aug. 4, 1892, a crime of epic proportions rocked Fall River, a bustling mill town in southeastern Massachusetts. Residents Andrew Borden and his second wife, Abby, were discovered bludgeoned to death inside their home on Second St.
The murder weapon? A hatchet.
Beyond its grisly nature, it was also an act of ruthless violence, considering Andrew Borden received nearly a dozen blows to his head and face. Abby Borden got 19.

That alone would have been notable, but when Andrew Borden's 32-year-old daughter, Lizzie, was charged in the crime, the case made headlines. And in the months that followed her stunning arrest, Lizzie Borden was tried — and acquitted — of murdering her father and stepmother in a courtroom drama rivaling the modern-day trials of O.J. Simpson or the Menendez brothers.

More than a century later, their deaths remain unsolved. But the case is being explored once again through Ian Brennan and Ryan Murphy’s anthology series “Monster,” which centers around the stories of real-life individuals whose gruesome actions have shaken the nation and made an indelible mark on history.

Ahead of the Sept. 17 release of Netflix’s “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” TODAY.com spoke with experts who help breakdown the facts, the myths and the ongoing appeal of the case — as well as offering their thoughts on who might ultimately be responsible for the murders of Andrew and Abby Borden.
Who Were the Bordens?

According to Michael Martins — curator of the Fall River Historical Society and author of “Parallel Lives: A Social History of Lizzie A. Borden and Her Fall River” — there was nothing particularly unique about the Borden family.
“If not for the events of August 4, 1892, they would have been completely lost to history,” he explains. “They would just be named in a city directory or nameless faces in a photograph.”

A self-made man, Andrew Borden became wealthy from his dealings in furniture and casket-making in the 1800s. A shrewd financier, he used the money to invest in stocks and real estate, amassing a fortune of roughly $300,000 at the time of his death. The fortune, Martins says, was a “considerable amount of money” at the time.

In 1845, he married Sarah Morse and the couple had three daughters, Emma, Alice (who died at the age of one) and Lizzie. Upon Sarah Morse Borden's death from uterine congestion at 39, Andrew Borden got remarried to Abby Durfee Gray in 1865.
After losing his first wife, Andrew remained friendly with her brother, John Morse, who was reported to have visited the family fairly often over the years.
"According to (Emma and Lizzie), he just sort of showed up from time to time and usually stayed in a room on the second or third floor," says Martins.
By 1892, Andrew, Abby, Emma and Lizzie still lived together in Andrew Borden's Fall River home, with the latter considered spinsters at the ages of 40 and 32, respectively.

There are conflicting accounts of Lizzie and Emma Borden's relationship with their father. Some suggest they were close, while others cite Andrew Borden as a stingy miser — forcing the family to use chamber pots instead of toilets, refusing to put central heat in the house, insisting that spoiled food be served at mealtimes — among other claims. According to Martins, however, there's little concrete evidence to back up those theories.

As far as Lizzie and Emma Borden's relationship with their stepmother, what might have been an amicable — if not necessarily warm — relationship soured in the late 1880s when Andrew Borden used a large portion of his fortune to purchase he second wife's family home.

"We know that from that point, both Lizzie and Emma blamed their stepmother for their father's actions. Even though he tried to equalize matters by deeding over some property to them, they viewed their stepmother as having played this negative role in siphoning away Borden money to (Abby's) family," explains Cara Robertson, former clerk for the U.S. Supreme Court, and author of the book “The Trial of Lizzie Borden.”
After that, Robertson says the Borden household was likely filled with a fair amount of "tension."
"Lizzie Borden famously was very forthright and she complained to people about her stepmother and that was sort of the 'not done' thing," she says.
Though no one knows for sure what went on behind the closed doors of the Borden house, one thing is certain: Andrew and Abby Borden were discovered dead after being violently murdered there.
What Exactly Happened on August 4, 1892?
It was a sweltering summer day in New England.

According to Martins, John Morse was visiting the Bordens in Fall River and joined them for breakfast on that fateful morning. After the meal ended, he left to visit family on the other side of town and Andrew Borden also left to take his morning walk. And Emma? She was out of town visiting relatives.
Left behind were Lizzie, Abby and the Borden's live-in housemaid, Bridget Sullivan.
According to the police inquest, Lizzie reported spending the morning reading magazines, folding laundry and ironing handkerchiefs before going out to the family's barn to look for fishing sinkers.
She returned and discovered her father’s body, according to testimony.
Lying on the living room couch was Andrew Borden, dead from repeated blows to his face and head. Upstairs Abby was found facedown on the floor of the guest room, a victim of the exact same fate.

"She appears to have been cornered between a bed and a bureau when she was taken out and she was struck repeatedly with a very small, shop-hatchet like weapon,” says Martins. “It was a brutal vicious crime.”

While some have speculated that the murders could have been a hit on the couple as retribution for business dealings gone wrong, Martins says that it seems unlikely that a hired killer would deliver the amount of blows the couple received.
"The crime clearly was perpetrated by someone who either was totally, totally insane or had some sort of vendetta against these people," says Martins.
Even more baffling, it was later determined by forensics that the murders occurred nearly two hours apart.

"So, did someone get into the house?” says Martins. “If they did, they managed to get in out and come back nearly two hours later. Or managed to get in and stayed in the house for that amount of time."

Given that the Borden house was located on a busy street, the killer would've also had to come and go unnoticed by neighbors and passersby. More than that, if they remained in the house, how did they go unnoticed for so long? Further adding to the mystery is that according to Martins, there was very little physical evidence.
"They managed to cover their tracks really, really well because there’s so little blood splattered about the house,” Martins said.
The Suspects
At the heart of the Borden murders is a deeply-complex whodunnit that has stumped experts for more than a century.
Among the suspects? The visiting John Morse, who claimed to be riding on a streetcar when the murders were committed.

"He remembered the badge number of the streetcar conductor or streetcar that he took, which seems sort of an odd thing for one to remember," says Martins. Even so, Martins says Morse was seen by many people that day and likely didn't stand to inherit in the event of Andrew Borden's death.
"But there were those who believed that if he did murder the Bordens, he might have been conspiring with the Borden sisters in order to take out Andrew and Abby," he says.

Then, there's Bridget Sullivan, the Irish housemaid who was in the house the day of the murders. According to Robertson, Abby Borden was the only member of the household to call her by her given name. Lizzie and Emma only ever referred to her only as “Maggie.”

“It does seemed pointed in this context,” says Robertson, explaining that even though they all lived together in a relatively small space, never learning Sullivan’s real name was “a pretty damning portrait of the people.”
Even so, Sullivan was ultimately ruled out as a suspect.

"We know the maid didn't come into any sizeable amount of money," says Martins. And after the murders, Sullivan left the Borden home, eventually settling in Montana and living a quiet life until her death in 1948.

Emma Borden was also considered a possible suspect. "Some people believe Emma Borden returned from the house party that she was at in Marion, Massachusetts and committed the crime; which sounds highly unlikely," says Martins.

And of course, the murders could have been committed by a random “crazed person,” disgruntled worker of Andrew Borden's or other unknown person, Martins said, adding that “it’s all up to speculation.”
Lizzie Borden Is Charged
While many people were questioned in connection with the crime, only one was charged: Lizzie Borden.

"If you read any of the trial testimony, the prosecution was saying that clearly Lizzie Borden hated her stepmother and hated her father and was concerned about the money and had every reason to want to see them dead. She was in the house, she was about the place at the time of the murders," says Martins.
The circumstantial evidence was also damning.

During her trial, the prosecution suggested the 32-year-old had attempted to poison her father and stepmother prior to Aug. 4, presenting witnesses who testified Lizzie Borden tried to purchase prussic acid, or cyanide, claiming she wanted to clean a sealskin cape with it – a fur that would have been hot and unwearable in the dead of summer.

Then there's the matter of a dress Lizzie Borden burned in the kitchen shortly after the murders occurred. It was a dress she said had paint on it and was doing due diligence in disposing of it. Police never found said dress.

"A painter and a dressmaker testified that she did, indeed, get paint on a dress," says Martin. But in the aftermath of a double murder, it seemed odd to set aside time to burn an unwanted dress, let alone a dress the police didn't note during their evidence collection.
Then again, maybe it just wasn't there.
"It does suggest that the dress was concealed between the time of the murders and the time that it was burned," says Robertson. "That looks bad for Lizzie Borden."
But in a drama-filled trial that held the world captive awaiting its verdict, Lizzie Borden was found not guilty. Was it because the all-male jury thought she was innocent or something else?

"The only penalty for murder was the death penalty," says Robertson. If Lizzie Borden had been convicted, she would have been hanged, something Robertson says the defense team used to seed doubt in the all-male jury's minds.
"'If you believe the prosecution, you're going to send this woman to her death, there's no alternative,'" she says that the defense reasoned. "And that must have weighed very heavily on them."
In the end, she was acquitted and returned to Fall River where she remained until her death in 1927.
So, Who Did It?
In the eyes of the court, Lizzie Borden was found innocent of the crime. Public opinion, however, was a different story.
For years after the not-guilty verdict, Lizzie Borden was still thought by many to be guilty of murdering her father and stepmother.
"She was relentlessly haunted by this spectrum of suspicion for the rest of her life," says Martins.
But the question of her guilt or innocence remains as ambiguous as it did more than one hundred years ago.

"If you believe she's guilty, then the difficulties of her life after the events of August 4, 1892, perhaps, were atonement for sins. But if you think by any stretch of the imagination that she might have been innocent, then, in her life, you're going to find the makings of an epic tragedy. So it's one extreme to the other, but there's nothing in between," says Martins.
Who does he think might have committed the crime?
"I have no idea who did it and I don't think anyone ever will know actually one way or the other," Martins says.

As for Robertson, she says that if the case went to trial today and she was given the choice between serving as prosecutor or defense attorney, Robertson says she'd choose to prosecute. But that doesn't mean she's convinced of Lizzie Borden's guilt, nor does it mean she has an inkling about who did it.
"You want to be the person who figures out the puzzle," says Robertson. "Spoiler alert – I don't solve the mystery."

title: Why Is Serial Killer Aileen Wuornos in ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story’?
summary: What does a female serial killer who was executed in 2002 have to do with a woman famously accused of killing her parents with a hatchet in 1892?
story: What does a female serial killer who was executed in 2002 have to do with a woman famously accused of killing her parents with a hatchet in 1892?

In the new Netflix series “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” showrunners Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan imply a connection between the infamous, late 19th Century figure and Aileen Wuornos, the convicted killer who inspired the Oscar-winning 2003 film “Monster.”
Emmy winner Sarah Paulson portrays Wuornos in the eighth episode of “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” which began streaming on Sept. 17.
Here’s what to know about Wuornos and her appearance on the Netflix show.
Who Was Aileen Wuornos?

Wuornos was born in 1956 and grew up in Michigan, where she endured a chaotic and abusive childhood. She said she was abandoned by her parents, routinely beaten and endured the deaths of family members, according to an archival prison interview with Wuornos in the 2025 Netflix documentary, “Aileen: Queen of the Serial Killers.”

In the same interview, said she ran away from home at 15 years old, hitchhiking and making a living as a sex worker for four years, during which she said she was raped about 30 times. Wuornos was 20 when she ended up in Florida and said she attempted to die by suicide when she shot herself through the stomach, but she survived, according to the documentary.
While in Florida, she began a relationship with hotel maid Tyria Moore, whom she supported with her earnings from sex work.

Beginning in 1989, Wuornos killed seven men across central Florida in a 12-month period. She was arrested in 1991 and confessed to the murders, claiming she did it in self-defense because the men had raped her and threatened to kill her. She later said in a 2000 interview that the claim of self-defense was a lie.
In 1992, she pleaded no contest to killing three of the men. She was sentenced to the death penalty and was executed by lethal injection in Florida in 2002.

Wuornos was labeled as one of the first high-profile female serial killers. Her supporters maintained that her traumatic abuse by men from the time she was a child drove her to become a cold-blooded killer.
“She is not a monster,” Wuornos’ adoptive mother, Arlene Pralle, says about Wuornos in the Netflix documentary. “She is a very caring, compassionate, feminine human being with a heart of gold.”

Charlize Theron won a Best Actress Oscar for her portrayal of Wuornos in the 2003 movie “Monster.” The movie depicts Wuornos arguing that she was fighting in self-defense by killing abusive male clients as a sex worker.
Why Is Aileen Wuornos in “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story”?
Paulson appears as Wuornos in the beginning and end of the final episode of “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.”

The two have no known connection in real life, as their stories occurred nearly a century apart. Borden was famously acquitted on charges of killing her parents, whereas Wuornos admitted to murdering multiple men.
The eighth episode of the Netflix show implies there is a similarity in the female rage that explodes in Wuornos and Borden.

“The show is exploring a legacy of female rage and reaction to the set of circumstances that they are presented with,” Ella Beatty, who plays Borden, told Netflix. “I think there’s a connection (between Borden and Wuornos) that Ryan and Ian were interested in mapping and exploring.”

That episode begins with Wuornos in a jailhouse interview, claiming she killed the men in self-defense. Wuornos is also portrayed on the stand in court, tearfully outlining the alleged brutality she endured at the hands of a man who hired her as a prostitute before she killed him.
She is then depicted talking to reporters outside a courthouse.
“Trying to defile my character, make me look like a monster, deranged or something like a Jeffrey Dahmer, which I’m not,” she says.
Wuornos’ death by lethal injection is also portrayed. She is shown speaking to a visitor ahead of her final moments.
“Just another woman put to death for something a man would’ve gotten away with,” she says.

The 1995 song “Carnival” by Natalie Merchant serves as a cinematic device. It plays while Wuornos is executed and then again at the end of Lizzie Borden’s story in the episode. Wuornos was a fan of Merchant’s and requested her music be played at her funeral, according to The New Yorker.
In a dream sequence, Wuornos is seen waking up on the table where she was executed. She sees Lizzie Borden and the Bordens’ housekeeper, Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan in the room.
“You’re going someplace safe,” Borden says. “All is forgiven. All is understood. At last.”
Beatty told Netflix that ultimately the two figures, Wuornos and Borden, serve as fascinating psychological subjects.

“Every season of Monster has been an exercise in understanding the person’s psychology,” she told the streaming service. “Are they born or are they made? I knew from the beginning that Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan were really interested in exploring what brings a woman to the point of violence.”

title: All the Movies on Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas 2026 Schedule
summary: What are the movies and TV shows on Hallmark's countdown to Christmas slate in 2026? Find out the names of the movies and when they come out.
story: The most wonderful time of year is almost here with less than 100 days until Christmas.

Hallmark will start spreading the Christmas cheer in one month, when their “Countdown to Christmas” programming kicks off in mid-October. Hallmark Channel recently marked its 25th birthday and for their commemorative year will release 34 original movies across 10 weeks. Their original series “Mistletoe Murders” is back for a third season to celebrate the joy of the holidays, too.
Autumn Reeser, who stars in this year’s “Christmas Delivered,” said there is a “sense of tradition” thanks to the holiday slate.

“(Fans) look forward to knowing us and knowing that we’re going to be there. There’s a sense of familiarity. There’s a sense of family. People feel like we are part of their holiday traditions. To know that I’m a part of millions of people’s holiday experiences — it kind of blows my mind,” she told TODAY.com at The 92nd Street Y in New York on Aug. 4. for the network’s 25-year celebration.

Hallmark alum Jonathan Bennett, who is in “Save the Date for Christmas,” said starring in the movies has made him love Christmas again. “For some people, Christmas isn’t such a great time. I lost both my parents the same year, so Christmases for about 10 years were really really painful, and then I found Hallmark Channel and started working with Hallmark Channel, and now I get excited about Christmas, and I get to give Christmas a new meaning and kind of a breath of fresh air for me, and it can mean something different now,” he said.
This year Hallmark is back with partnerships to bring memorable original films and exclusive products to viewers.

“The worlds and cultures of the NFL, Walt Disney World Resort, and Biltmore present special opportunities for us to bring fans unique tales of romance, family and community that are sure to be highlights of this holiday season,” Darren Abbott, president and Hallmark Media and Hallmark chief brand officer said in the “Countdown to Christmas” release.
The third installment of Hallmark Channel’s collaboration with the NFL and Skydance Sports will be “Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story.”

The relationship between Hallmark and The Walt Disney Company dates back to 1931 and this year they are releasing their first original movie together, “Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True,” which filmed at Walt Disney World Resort in Florida.

“A Biltmore Christmas” was a hit 2023 movie and this year the network is going back to the Biltmore Estate for the new movie, “A Grand Biltmore Christmas,” which once again was filmed at America’s largest home.

Andie MacDowell’s first Hallmark ‘Countdown to Christmas’ movie for the network will be “A Grand Biltmore Christmas.” She told TODAY.com, “It’s a great script. It’s a beautiful script, and I’m really looking forward for everybody to see it. It’s fantastic.”
Below, find a complete list of Hallmark’s festive TV programming that you will want to check twice, as the countdown to the holiday season begins.
Friday, Oct. 16

Description from Hallmark: “Hyper organized single mom and party planner Lexi (Amanda Schull), her free-spirited mother June (Barbara Niven) and teen daughter Piper (Verity Marks) are set to spend Christmas at a local ski resort after Lexi is hired to organize their annual holiday party.  Upon arrival she immediately butts heads with Ridge (Victor Webster), the ski instructor and son of the lodge’s owner, Dan (John B. Lowe).  Despite not getting along from the get-go, Lexi and Ridge notice a spark between June and Dan and decide to set them up.  Lexi and Ridge create a multitude of festive excursions — and excuses — to bring them together but thanks to creative machinations by June and Dan these outings keep turning into foursomes.  In the days leading up to the Christmas party Lexi and Ridge’s attempt to pair up their parents brings them closer together and their merry matchmaking ends in surprising results.”
Saturday, Oct. 17

Description from Hallmark: “When  ambitious  freelance  reporter  Avery  Clark  (Lyndsy Fonseca)  returns  to  Chicago  to  spend  Christmas with her mom (Barbara Alyn Woods) and new stepdad (Khary Payton), she’s hoping for a little holiday downtime before  her  next  assignment.    Instead,  she  lands  a  feel-good  story  profiling  Darlene  Donnelly  (Marsha Mason),  a  beloved  Chicago  Bears  superfan  about  to  celebrate  an  incredible  milestone  —  attending  her  500th  game. There’s  just  one  catch:  Avery  knows next  to  nothing  about football or  Chicago.  Enter  Darlene’s handsome grandson Matt (Robert Buckley), a Chicago firefighter and die-hard Bears fan who, with  a little gentle nudging from Darlene, agrees to show Avery what being part of Bears Nation is all about.  As Avery follows Darlene’s remarkable story through cherished game-day traditions, festive Chicago  adventures  and  memories  of  a  love  story  that  began  at  a  stadium,  she  starts  to  understand  that  football is about much more than what happens on the field.   And as sparks fly between Avery and  Matt, this Christmas may just convince a woman who’s always on the move that sometimes the greatest adventure is finding a place, and someone, that feels like home.”

Featured Cameos: Chicago Bears Head Coach Ben Johnson, quarterback Caleb Williams, tight end Colston Loveland, tight end Cole Kmet, legendary Bears alumni Mike Singletary, Charles “Peanut” Tillman and Dan Hampton, Connie Payton, wife of the late Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton, and the team’s beloved mascot Staley Da Bear, as well as Tamera Mowry-Housley, Marilu Henner, Jake Connelly and Dyon “Mojo” Brooks.

Marilu Henner discussed her cameo with TODAY.com, “I got to use my Chicago accent, so that was really fun. It’s always an adventure. There’s always something very special about each cast, about each director. When you do a Christmas movie, you cannot believe what it looks like. But it’s always beautiful and wonderful and heartfelt.”
Sunday, Oct. 18

Description from Hallmark: “Taylor Lewis (Brendan Penny) is a single dad and holiday display expert who relocates to the charming town of  Pineway with his two children just weeks before Christmas. Despite the challenges of a new home, new school and a daughter who seems to be outgrowing their cherished holiday traditions he’s determined to make the season magical. As Taylor takes charge of the town’s beloved Christmas Market revival, he finds himself unexpectedly partnered with Sophie Shaw (Pascale Hutton), a practical accountant hoping to prove she’s ready for a new leadership role. Together, the unlikely duo brings fresh ideas, festive spirit and plenty of Christmas cheer to the community.  But when Taylor’s well-intentioned efforts to help his teenage daughter backfire, he begins to realize that yuletide can’t be forced, it has to be discovered. As Taylor and Sophie grow closer, they learn that embracing change may be the key to creating new traditions and new memories.”
Friday, Oct. 23

Description from Hallmark: “Audrey Bell (Ashley Newbrough) is a globe-trotting pop-up restaurateur who returns home for Thanksgiving to the news that her late grandfather’s beloved bowling alley, Wonderlanes, will be sold. Audrey agrees to stay for one last festive season at Wonderlanes and decides to revive its iconic Winter Wonderlanes youth bowling tournament.  To drum up publicity for the event, she reluctantly teams up with Jason Miller (Franco Lo Presti), a local news reporter and her high school boyfriend. Working side by side the embers of their past start flickering, rekindling feelings they thought they left behind.  As the tournament draws near, Audrey questions her next move that will take her away from the people and places she loves...and decide if she’s ready to walk away from Wonderlanes — or finally put down roots where her heart truly belongs.”
Saturday, Oct. 24

Description from Hallmark: “Kathryn Liu (Janel Parrish) is an antiques buyer for her father’s store and has been happily dating Rob Ashford (Daniel Lissing) for nearly a year. When he surprises her with a pre- Christmas proposal, her fear of a failed relationship sends her dashing away without giving him an answer. Heartbroken, as Rob drives to his sister’s house he has a car accident that leaves him without memories of the past year, including their relationship and his once — infectious love of Christmas. Following the unconventional orders from his doctor, Kathryn agrees to help trigger Rob’s memory by retracing their romance and reintroducing him to the holidays. But as his memories inch closer to returning, Kathryn must face the painful truth that bringing Rob back to himself may mean losing him forever, unless she can finally find the courage to fight for the love she was too afraid to claim.”
Sunday, Oct. 25

Description from Hallmark: “Erin (Lori Loughlin) has always supported her heart surgeon husband, Adam’s (Tom Cavanagh) career by organizing the hospitals’ Christmas charity galas.  However, when he moves to a new hospital, her help is no longer needed. Feeling lost and without a purpose back in New York City, her long- suppressed regrets over giving up her dream of pursuing fashion design start bubbling up. When Erin is given a peculiar heart-shaped Christmas ornament, she wakes up in an alternate reality where she’s a world-famous fashion designer. As she “meets” and attends Christmas events with alternate universe Adam, she realizes that while her fashion dreams came true, it’s lonely at the top. While working on a way to bring more charity and heart to her fashion empire, she learns that her dream life and love were always right in front of her — if only she finds the heart and courage to ask.”
Friday, Oct. 30

Description from Hallmark: “Having recently relocated, Julie (Rhiannon Fish) is setting up her new town using pieces she inherited from her late grandmother, including a beautiful dining room table she plans to use on Christmas Eve when she hosts dinner for the first time. Though she doesn’t have her guest list set just yet Julie takes inspiration from her grandmother and has faith that her holiday table for eight will be filled. Julie’s warm, friendly nature leads her to quickly become part of the community and make friends, including her neighbor Mark (Jake Foy) and his young daughter Vanessa (Mila Morgan). Mark suggests that he and his family could join her, making Julie’s dream of dinner for eight come true.  But when bad weather keeps them from making the trip it looks like it will be a silent night with just the three of them unless a small Christmas miracle — or series of miracles — fills her holiday table.”
Saturday, Oct. 31

Description from Hallmark: “Maren (Amy Groening) is a busy single mother to her adopted daughter, Leah (Taylor Blake). As the owner of her late father’s beloved hardware store, she is often found helping repair just about anything for her fellow locals, leaving very little time for herself. When the chance to participate in the Christmas Companions program at Jolly Acres, a new-yet-thriving retirement community in town, Leah excitedly jumps at the chance as she misses having a grandfather in her life. Much to Leah’s delight, she is paired with Kris (Randy Apostle), a jolly resident who bears an uncanny resemblance to Santa Claus. While there, Maren crosses paths with the nomadic Reid (Michael Rady), the center’s Director of Community Launch and Operations whose job has him traveling from facility to facility to launch new branches. But the Christmas Companions program is soon jeopardized as the contractor for the center’s community room suddenly pulls out.  Seeing how much joy the program brings Leah and Kris, the always helpful Maren offers to help finish the project. As she spends more time at the center with Reid, Maren slowly realizes it’s okay to let others in, accept help and stop shouldering the entire load. Reid starts questioning whether to accept his next assignment which will take him far away from the people and center that have begun to feel like home. With the help of some Christmas magic — and a little assist from Kris– everyone finds where they belong.”
Sunday, Nov. 1

Description from Hallmark: “Marie (Emilie Ullerup) is a hotel tech executive living in Chicago who returns home to Copenhagen to spend the holidays with her family and puts herself to work at their inn. When Ryan Miller (Corey Sevier) checks in a case of mistaken identity leads Marie to believe he’s a travel writer. She sets out to make sure his stay is perfect, which includes the Christmas tour Ryan’s expecting ... but the Andersen Inn hasn’t offered it since her father passed so she scrambles to cobble together an itinerary meant to impress. When Marie’s mom tells her she plans to sell the inn after the New Year Marie becomes doubly determined to make Ryan’s visit a success — a positive story could boost business and convince her to keep the inn. Marie escorts Ryan on a carefully curated tour of Copenhagen and pulls out all the stops to create hygge at the inn, though both efforts end in some festive fiascos. Despite the mishaps the two forge a connection that may be more than just inn-keeper and tourist. When Ryan Miller the journalist arrives they realize their mistake, sending Marie into overdrive to ensure he experiences the perfect Danish Christmas. In the process, Marie learns that warmth, connection — and, possibly, romance — happen naturally and can’t be created.”
Thursday, Nov. 5

Description from Hallmark: “Emily Lane (Sarah Drew) once again teams up with Detective Sam Wilner (Peter Mooney) to solve three new Christmas mysteries as her past collides with her present, leaving her questioning everything she believed to be true.”
Catherine Bell and Holly Robinson Peete guest star in this season.
Friday, Nov. 6

Description from Hallmark: “Michaela (Lindura) is a rigid accountant who steps in to help her brother care for his young son Danny (Omi Fitzpatrick-Gonzales) while Danny’s military mom is deployed over Christmas. When Danny is assigned to create a holiday scrapbook for his mom, Michaela reluctantly accepts help from his free-spirited substitute teacher, Bryan (Brendan Morgan), whose creativity clashes with her need for preciseness and control. As they set out to capture festive moments for the scrapbook unexpected mishaps turn into meaningful traditions — and sparks begin to fly. Through Danny’s project, Michaela learns to embrace imperfection and open her heart, while Bryan rethinks his future as a traveling substitute teacher.”
Saturday, Nov. 7

Description from Hallmark: “Sally (Nikki DeLoach), an art teacher, has spent the last 10 years honoring the memory of her late husband Jake while raising their children, Keegan (Brandon Ironside) and Boo (Remy Marthaller). Feeling like she’s finally ready for love, she joins a dating app and is matched with Damon (Juan Pablo Di Pace), her former colleague  who  taught  her  kids’  kindergarten class. Jake had co-founded  a web platform  that preserved family home videos. When a server migration wipes out Sally’s treasured videos of him — and her phone containing backup copies accidentally shatters — the only hope is finding the original tapes. She doesn’t want Keegan and Boo to know about the missing videos so to buy time until they’re recovered, Sally institutes a screen-free Christmas for her family while secretly searching for the tapes. After she connects with Damon at his uncle’s antique store, he joins the hunt and the two grow closer.  Keegan and Boo soon discover the joys of unplugging and spending quality time with their grandparents, who also come around and embrace the experiment after begrudgingly agreeing. With every lead exhausted, Sally is forced to admit the videos may be gone forever. As the fate of the tapes is in flux, the family learns the importance of cherishing old memories and creating new ones.”
Sunday, Nov. 8

Description from Hallmark: “Heidi (Brooke D’Orsay) and Sophie (Ali Liebert) are sisters who couldn’t be more different — Heidi is buttoned-up and laser focused on landing the play-by-play job for the local pro hockey team while Sophie is following her dream of making it in stand-up comedy while waitressing.  Though a years-ago rift following their mother’s passing have pulled the sisters apart, what they do share is a deep love for their father Ed (James Denton). When a fainting episode lands him in the hospital Heidi and Sophie rush to his side.  Hating seeing their father in that state — and still alone four years after losing their mother — the sisters decide to set aside their differences and team up to play Cupid at Christmas. As Heidi and Sophie work together to prepare Ed for the dating world in the hope he’ll find someone special in time for the holiday, they each go on their own journeys that bring them unexpected joy, love and peace for Christmas.”
Friday, Nov. 13

Description from Hallmark: “Meg (Amy Acker) set aside her newscaster aspirations after a disastrous audition experience in college and has been happy as a news producer in her small town of Fern, Texas.  Billy Kane (Luke Macfarlane), her former college crush and audition partner, is a well-known celebrity host in Hollywood on the brink of losing his career after an on-camera gaffe.  At the advice of his publicist, Billy begrudgingly returns to Texas to lay low and spend the holidays with his sister (Sara Canning) and her family. When Meg and Billy cross paths he’s happy to see her but her feelings are on the frostier side — she’s still upset he took advantage of her failed audition to get the gig himself.  Meg finds herself seeing Billy more than she’d like since his nephew Graham (Isaiah Haegert) is in the horse therapy program her dad runs at their ranch.  With their annual Reindeer Roundup holiday event coming up Meg’s dad gets sidelined after an injury. Her dad enlists Billy to serve as its host, much to Meg’s chagrin. With the Reindeer Roundup just days away, Meg teaches Billy basic riding and roping skills to get him ready for his hosting duties. In the process, they slowly reconnect and Meg sees there’s more to him than Hollywood glitz.  As their connection grows, each of them helps give the other the courage to step outside their comfort zones and find new joy — and possibly love — in unexpected ways.”
Saturday, Nov. 14

Description from Hallmark: “One Christmas Eve Marty (Tyler Hynes), whose life is in a bit of a rut, finds himself wishing he had more time. Thanks to some holiday magic, he awakes the next morning to discover it’s Christmas Eve — again. Confused at first, Marty learns to embrace his new normal and begins to truly appreciate the sights, sounds and people of New York City that previously went unnoticed. With this gift of time, he expands  his  world  by  learning  how  to  play  a  new  instrument,  picking  up  new  languages  and reading...every single book. But when Marty meets Chloe (Laci J Mailey), a newly out-of-work journalist having a tough day, he falls hard for her. The only problem is that when the morning of December 24 comes once again,  she  doesn’t  know  who  he  is. As  the  Christmas  Eves continue  to repeat themselves, Marty makes it his mission to win her over and , in the process, figure out what he needs to do to finally make his way to Christmas Day — hopefully with Chloe by his side.”
Sunday, Nov. 15

Description from Hallmark: “Claire Bennett (Tamera Mowry-Housley) is a successful business consultant in Manhattan who unexpectedly inherits her beloved Uncle Lou’s Christmas-themed bar, The Tipsy Reindeer, in upstate New York. When she returns, Claire discovers the bar comes with high debt–her Uncle Lou was overly generous to people in town while the booming business of Algorithm, an upscale and trendy new club, added insult to injury. She intends to turn things around before Christmas and sell to someone who will preserve her uncle’s legacy and then return to her life in the city. Claire meets Zach (Kristoffer Polaha), Algorithm’s part owner and manager, who tells her they want to buy The Tipsy Reindeer so they can expand. Claire bristles at the proposition and they agree to face off in a 12 Days of Christmas- inspired series of festive events to see who can bring in the most business — if Claire wins, Zach will use his contacts to find the right buyer but if Zach emerges victorious, Claire agrees to consider Algorithm’s offer. As they compete over the course of the 12 days their attraction is undeniable. Rivalry leads to romance and the two are faced with figuring out how their shifting priorities might somehow lead them down the same road, together.”
Friday, Nov. 20

Description from Hallmark: “When Lexi Bell (Taylor Cole) returns home for the holidays, she faces a beloved family tradition she’d rather avoid: the fiercely competitive Bell Bowl, an annual Christmas flag football showdown between her father and uncle that has fueled decades of sibling rivalry.  But when an injury sidelines her brother-in-law it looks like Lexi’s family’s losing streak will remain unbroken.  To give them a fighting chance, she strikes a deal with Eddie (Charles Michael Davis), a former local football star-turned teacher — Lexi will use her baking know-how to help Eddie best his brother in their annual bake-off if he’ll pose as her boyfriend and meet the “eligibility requirement” to play on their team.  As they navigate each other’s festive family gatherings, traditions and celebrations, what started as a transactional partnership begins to become something more as Lexi and Eddie find themselves feeling less and less like their romantic relationship is just pretend.  As the two clans battle it out on the field, regardless of who takes home the trophy Lexi may have already won at love.”
Saturday, Nov. 21

Description from Hallmark: “On-set veterinarian Goldie MacKenzie (Erin Cahill) leaves the glamour of Hollywood behind to buy a family-run veterinary clinic in tight-knit Blue Dog Valley, arriving just in time for the town’s cherished Christmas season.  When Dr. Gable, the clinic’s longtime owner, unexpectedly ends up out of town, Goldie is hosted by his handsome son Cohen (Andrew Walker), the black sheep of the family because he decided to forego their expectation of becoming a vet.  Cohen and Goldie get off on the wrong foot, but when the folks of Blue Dog Valley cold shoulder “the newcomer,” Cohen teams up with Goldie to win over even the frostiest of community members. Goldie is also aided by the mysterious canine she dubs Blue whose spontaneous appearances always seem to guide Goldie to exactly where she needs to be. As Goldie works hard to prove herself to the townspeople when furry and Christmas crises arise, she finds herself pulled towards the very heart of her new-found home ... and a certain black sheep.”
Saturday, Nov. 22

Description from Hallmark: “There’s only one thing identical twins, quiet and bookish Abigail (Rachael Leigh Cook) and globe-trotting event planner Charlie (Rachael Leigh Cook), agree on is that this first Christmas without their mom will be difficult. When they unexpectedly get a last-minute chance to travel to Wales and spend a week running the Story Shoppe, an AirBnb/bookshop in Hay-on-Wye, they jump at the opportunity. Abigail is particularly excited, given the town’s role as the backdrop of the bestselling Winterton Chronicles, her all-time favorite Regency holiday romances. Upon arrival, Abigail dives into setting up the bookshop’s window display with help from the friendly next-door barista, Tom (Owain Yeoman), who is also a fan of the Winterton Chronicles. Meanwhile, Charlie meets the dashing Lord Rhys (Stephen Hagan), the great-nephew of Evelyn Calon, who wrote the book series. Abigail is charmed by a series of thoughtful Christmas ornaments she assumes are from Rhys (but are actually from Tom), while Charlie and Rhys grow closer as they help plan the Winterton Ball at Rhys’ castle. Mistaken identities lead to a series of merry mix-ups as Rhys and Tom woo the sisters, unaware they are twins. On the night of the ball, however, the sisters’ double secret is discovered. As the truth is unwrapped, the crisscrossed lovers discover that the perfect holiday happy ending isn’t always by the book.”
Thursday, Nov. 26

Description from Hallmark: “Determined to unwind from the stresses and loneliness of her everyday life, Kimberly Carr (Autumn Reeser) travels to Canada to spend Christmas with her grandmother, JoJo (Linda Darlow), at her beautiful, cozy farmhouse. Kimberly’s plans for a restorative holiday are turned upside down when she crosses paths with Ben Chambers (Wes Brown), owner of a local tree farm and new Christmas tree delivery app called TreeBen. Ben’s a dreamer who never looks before he leaps while Kimberly is methodical and lives her life based on practicality — the two couldn’t be more different. But when Ben’s app is plagued by an onslaught of issues, Kimberly uses her tech expertise to help him out and ensure that no one in town is deprived of a Christmas tree...even though she isn’t convinced of the need for the app in such a small town. As they team up to deliver trees in his red truck, Kimberly and Ben discover they may have more in common than they realized. In the process, Kimberly begins to question if she’s truly happy with her life or if she’s ready for a change and — just maybe — ready for romance.”
Friday, Nov. 27

Description from Hallmark: “Silvana “Silvy” Gianetti (Daniella Monet) is disillusioned with her job as the Executive Chef at a swanky restaurant in New York.  Growing up in a large and loving Italian-American family, Silvy is drawn to the food and comfort of her home.  When her beloved Nonna suffers a minor wrist injury, Silvy is called back home to Boston’s Italian North End to prepare the family’s beloved “Feast of the Seven Fishes” Christmas Eve dinner.  As she preps for the big feast, her family is joined by Ethan (Kevin McGarry), a photographer who is documenting different family traditions around town and who’s become close to her Nonna.  After a rocky start with Ethan, things begin to heat up as Silvy grows to appreciate the heart and soul he puts into capturing the magic of the little moments and a romance could be simmering.  Every day leading up to Christmas Eve, Silvy gathers in the kitchen with her Nonna, mom and aunt to prepare the pasta, struffoli and other Italian classics near and dear to Silvy’s heart.  This special family time reminds her of the kind of cooking that truly brings her joy and leads Silvy to rethink where she belongs and gets a clear picture of who should be by her side.”
This film is executive produced by Giada DeLaurentiis.
Friday, Nov. 27

Description from Hallmark: “Hopeful  and dreamy 8-year-old  Jake  (Paul Campbell)  writes  a  letter  to  Santa  with  all  his  most fantastical wishes. But when the letter gets lost in the North Pole, young Jake wakes up disappointed, and no longer a believer. Decades later Santa discovers the misplaced letter and immediately sets out to make things right. Now an adult, Jake’s life is about to get turned upside down when the appearance of his childhood wishes clash with his practical life. All while his childhood best friend Julie (Rachel Boston) rather unexpectedly moved back to town. As Santa continues to check off Jake’s list, Jake and Julie combine forces to anticipate each new wishes’ chaotic consequences, all while growing closer to each other–and possibly leading Jake closer to his most important childhood dream.”
Saturday, Nov. 28

Description from Hallmark: “Every Christmas, a small town honors the memory of a beloved teacher who once spread joy through her ‘Secret Norma’ gifts each holiday by creating a whimsical and heartfelt scavenger hunt for one worthy recipient. When burned-out art teacher Vanessa (Tammin Sursok) visits her widowed brother and niece Esther for the holidays, she is surprised to be chosen as the next ‘Secret Norma’ recipient. Hoping to bring Esther some Christmas magic, Vanessa decides to help revive the town’s holiday block party.  Her handsome electrician neighbor Spencer (Peter Porte) offers help with the preparations if Vanessa will help him sell his mother Norma’s house.  As Vanessa solves the riddles of ‘Secret Norma’ and plans the block party, her passion for teaching art begins to spark along with her feelings for the charming electrician next door.”
Saturday, Nov. 28

Description from Hallmark: “Lindsey (Lacey Chabert) and her extended family head to the Walt Disney World Resort® to spend a magical Christmas together.  But the dream of a jolly holiday gets quickly dashed when Lindsey discovers her room is next door to Philip (Travis Van Winkle), a disastrous first date she recently had, who’s also there on a family trip. As Lindsey and Philip’s paths cross throughout their stay, the frost starts to thaw as they learn they’re not so different from each other after all.  Thanks to some Walt Disney World magic, the holiday wish  Lindsey made  in  Cinderella  Fountain just might turn their  rivalry into romance.”
Richard Kind, Christy Carlson Romano, Bryce Durfee, and Taegen Burns also star in this movie.

Lacey Chabert told TODAY.com, “I feel like this year personally was full of pinch me moments — getting to film at Disney World for a ‘Holiday Ever After.’ There’s something about like a childhood dream come true and feeling like a kid again. And I think the nostalgia of that is what is infused into the Hallmark Christmas movies that really resonates with people. I know it does with me.”
Sunday, Nov. 29

Description from Hallmark: “Hannah (Hunter King), who works for a large auction house in New York City, is excited for her best friend Ethan (Dan Jeannotte) to return home for a visit during Hannukah and is looking forward to some much-needed time off from work  That plan is short lived when Ethan shares the news that he’s convinced the daughter of his wealthy boss to use Hannah’s auction house to sell their family’s collection of Judaica with the condition that Hannah handles the sale.  Complicating her holiday further, she meets the mysterious Pearl (Felicia Shulman), who gifts her with an antique menorah that is anything but ordinary as it takes her back to a different times of her life each night of Hanukkah, with Pearl as her guide.  This front row seat past moments — including some that involve Ethan — leads Hannah to reflect, break out of her comfort zone and overcome her fear of failure.  Thanks to her trips through the past, and as she and Ethan spend time together in the present Hannah realizes she has feelings for him she never acknowledged.  Through this journey, Hannah makes some bold decisions about her life — and love — that are sure to make this Hanukkah one to remember.”
Sunday, Nov. 29

Description from Hallmark: “When an early snowstorm sweeps through the Midwest, punctual, straight-laced “suit” Cassidy Fields (Ashley Williams) is  forced  to  hitch  a  ride  with  free  spirited,  music  loving  Johanna “Jo”  Woods (Alison Sweeney) in her brother Chase’s (Steve Lund) 18-wheeler to the nearest airport to catch another flight. However, when Jo’s flight successfully takes off and Cassidy’s is cancelled again at the last minute, she joins Chase on the road back to Tennessee from Chicago to make it home in time to spend Christmas with her father. Quickly, Cassidy and Chase’s connection begins to spark. Through losing the car keys, stopping to partake in a Mrs. Claus parade and a surprise run-in with Jo, whose plane got grounded mid-flight due to weather, Cassidy builds bonds with both siblings as they all challenge one another’s life philosophies. As the trio pushes past every obstacle, they work to embrace their differences and find that the fastest way home is when they lean on one another for help.”
Friday, Dec. 4

Description from Hallmark: “When driven corporate attorney Tanya (Heather Hemmens) rushes into a charming gift shop searching for a last-minute White Elephant gift, she crosses paths with Jason (Mark Ghanimé), a handsome, laid-back clerk.  Their brief encounter leads Tanya to purchase a beautiful antique glass snowflake which, unbeknownst to her or Jason, is a good luck charm that carries a generations-old Christmas tradition. However, since the ornament is entered into a holiday gift exchange rather than gifted with proper intention, Tanya suddenly finds herself on the receiving end of everyone else’s misfortune. After Jason’s Aunt Coco (Jayne Eastwood) explains the snowflake’s magical lore, Tanya reluctantly teams up with Jason to track down the snowflake as it makes its way from one recipient to the next across Chicago before Christmas Day or she’ll be stuck with bad luck until next Christmas.  Along the way, the  pair  is  swept  into  festive  holiday  adventures,  unexpected  encounters  and  a  journey  that challenges Tanya’s carefully structured life.  As they race against the clock to undo the snowflake’s magic, Tanya and Jason’s relationship turns into something more and they may find that their biggest stroke of luck was meeting each other.”
Saturday, Dec. 5

Description from Hallmark: “As Biltmore House opens for the first time on Christmas Eve 1895, 13-year-old Elizabeth and her family are holiday guests.  When she notices Michael, a fellow teen caught trespassing by the staff, Elizabeth comes to his rescue by claiming to know him, much to his relief.  The two share an instant connection and set out to explore Biltmore but Michael inexplicably vanishes. Twenty years later, Elizabeth  (Holland Roden)  is  spending  Christmas  at  Biltmore  and  this  time  is accompanied  by  James (James Trevena), a suitor her Aunt Maysilee (Andie MacDowell), is keen for her to wed.  When a stranger asks Elizabeth to dance at the Christmas gala she’s shocked to discover it’s Michael (Niall Matter).  Thrilled to reunite with her friend, she throws herself into his arms.  But the world around her changes in an instant when Elizabeth is transported into the modern world with Michael, a tourist from the present day who had traveled to the past 20 years prior with the help of a magical hourglass in Biltmore’s library.  Now, Elizabeth and Michael must find a way to send her back to her time, while not arousing the suspicion of Michael’s mother and sister during their family vacation.  As Elizabeth experiences life and Christmas in the 21st century, she and Michael become close.  When the time comes for her to return to 1915, Elizabeth must decide whether she’ll resume the life that’s been chosen for her or if her heart will lead her down a new path in the present.”
Jonathan Frakes, Rachel Boston, and Wes Brown also star in this movie.
Saturday, Dec. 5

Description from Hallmark: “Join hosts Jonathan Bennett and Melissa Peterman and other favorite stars at Hallmark’s Christmas Experience and get an exclusive look at what’s coming to Hallmark in 2027.”
Sunday, Dec. 6

Description from Hallmark: “Amanda (Fiona Gubelmann) and Jack (Marco Grazzini) had a whirlwind romance and got married after knowing each other for only three months. Their first — and only — Christmas together was calamitous and was the beginning of the end to their brief marriage.  Three years post-divorce and still harboring an aversion for the holiday, Amanda is heading to Vermont with her sister Lucy (Siobhan Williams) to enjoy an un-Christmasy getaway...and finds that Jack is on their flight.  En route, Amanda meets Margaret (Nancy Robertson), a quirky traveler who disappears without a trace and without being seen by anyone else, leaving Amanda mystified.  Bad weather diverts the plane to the remote town of Pinecone Lake, leaving Amanda with the last person she wants to be stranded with — Jack. Shortly after arriving, Margaret inexplicably reappears and convinces a confused Amanda that she is in fact her guardian angel and has been her entire life.  As the days leading to Christmas pass by, Amanda slowly begins to feel connected to the community and, with Margaret’s guidance, sees beyond past circumstances and follows her heart to where — and with whom — she truly belongs.”
Friday, Dec. 11

Description from Hallmark: “Rose (Jessy Schram) arrives in Canterbury, England eager to spend the holidays with her childhood friend Asha (Sohm Kapila) as she leaves behind her hometown of Vienna, OH following the passing of her beloved Grandma Bud. Having first met in a children’s choir they went on to pursue careers as choir masters. As Rose arrives Asha is put on bed rest in the final days of her pregnancy. Rose steps in when the headmistress offers her the job...not realizing there was confusion over which Vienna children’s choir she worked with. Rose’s “glass half full” attitude is tested when she crosses paths with Harrison (Will Kemp), the traditionalist boys’ choir master who has an unwavering allegiance to history and precedents. The boys’ choir always performs at the annual Christmas Eve concert in Canterbury Cathedral but Rose questions why the girls don’t have the opportunity. When the school’s headmistress decides the two choirs should compete against each other for the honor, they get to work to prepare their students. Along the way, their rivalry sparks a romance and these two seemingly opposites from opposite sides of the pond discover they may not be so different after all.”
Saturday, Dec. 12

Description from Hallmark: “Inspired by Brad Paisley’s song “Snow Globe Town,” this heartfelt holiday romance follows Emily Church (Kimberley Sustad), who joins her sister Zoe and Zoe’s longtime boyfriend on a Christmas getaway to Pine Grove, the town famously known as the Christmas Proposal Capital of America.  Expecting to help capture a photos of Zoe’s perfect engagement moment as is their family’s tradition, Emily instead finds herself unexpectedly sidelined by the town’s couples-only traditions and paired with Bert Baxter (Scott Michael Foster), a skeptical journalist researching the celebrated romantic legacy inspired by his grandfather.  As Emily quietly works behind the scenes to help Zoe’s proposal plans come together, she and  Bert are  drawn into the  town’s  festive  traditions,  holiday  competitions  and  Christmas celebrations.  Along the way they discover a shared outlook on love and life that challenges both of their expectations.  As old assumptions are tested and new possibilities emerge, Pine Grove reminds them that love, family and the spirit of Christmas often arrive in the most unexpected ways.”
Sunday, Dec. 13

Description from Hallmark: “Before they can embark on their luxurious Hawaiian holiday, uptight sports medicine physician Joseph (Benjamin Ayres) and his daughter Annie (Kaelyn Yoon-MacRae) must first begrudgingly make a pit stop at a remote campground and deliver a package from his late father to a mysterious person named Birdie.  Their plans are derailed when Joseph accidentally crashes into free-spirited Nora’s (Torrey DeVitto) RV at a rest stop.  Things go from bad to worse when they not only fail to find the elusive Birdie, but their ancient Winnebago breaks down as well.  Forced to spend the next few days at the campground while they wait for replacement parts, Nora introduces Joseph and Annie to the eccentric campers who lovingly dub themselves the Nomads.  The embers of romance begin to glow as Nora shows Joseph how to embrace the freedom of camp life.  When the mystery of who Birdie is becomes clearer and the much-awaited parts arrive allowing Joseph and Annie to finally make their Hawaiian getaway, Joseph must decide if leaving the campground and person who makes it feel more like home is in the plans.”
Friday, Dec. 18

Description from Hallmark: “Mari (Mishael Morgan) is a fiercely intelligent music historian who manages to get an invite to the annual Christmas gala for the local music museum and has one goal: secure an interview with Tasha (Holly Robinson Peete) the legendary Grammy award-winning singer, record producer, and museum’s founder. Mari has to summon the courage to ask the mogul who rarely does interviews these days for this favor, which proves more difficult than anticipated. Also crashing the gala is Julian (B.J. Britt), a polished and perpetually busy New York attorney on a mission of his own – his late mother received the autograph of Nat King Cole on a piece of sheet music when she was a young girl and he regrettably donated this treasured piece of family history to the DuPree Museum while emotionally numb in the aftermath of his mother’s death. Now his sister tells him she wants to give the framed sheet music to her daughter/his niece, who inherited her grandmother’s musical talent, for Christmas and Julian is determined to bring it back home. When Mari and Julian cross paths at the gala, they ultimately team up as they look for their chance to talk to the elusive host while participating in increasingly chaotic Christmas contests whose winners will get a tour of the museum that night by Tasha herself. What neither of them expects is how their partnership deepens over the course of this unforgettable evening and leads them to discover that what they were searching for isn’t necessarily what they actually need.”
Saturday, Dec. 19

Description from Hallmark: “Billie (Tori Anderson) is a workaholic realtor who heads home for Christmas but her journey is derailed after loveable, but chaotic canine named Yappy almost causes her car to crash.  After talking to Yappy’s owner, the mysterious, yet oddly familiar Mrs. C, Billie agrees to watch Yappy while she visits her grandchildren for the holidays. Yappy ends up playing the role of matchmaker and new best friend, pulling Billie towards her traveling contractor ex-boyfriend from high school, Hutch (Ian Harding). Eager to move on she’s determined to leave Hutch in the past, but when her mother hires him to work on their shed, she finds herself spending more time with him than she ever expected. As the holidays draw closer, Billie begins to question whether chasing her dream of becoming her firm’s number one seller is truly what she wants. When the mysterious Mrs. C leaves her cabin for Billie and Hutch to breathe new life into, her answer may come sooner than expected.”
Sunday, Dec. 20

Description from Hallmark: “Susie (Italia Ricci) has checked out on dating while Alec (Jonathan Bennett) is a hopeless romantic — these longtime friends have both struck out in the love department after failing to meet the right man. After being each other’s plus one to what feels like the twentieth wedding this year, they vow to take a break from attending weddings and looking for their respective prince charming. That break doesn’t last long as next day Susie’s sister announces a last-minute Christmas wedding...and Susie convinces Alec to tag along. The objective for the week? Survive as the two lone, single people and avoid family matchmaking. Over time, the Christmas wedding duties and time with family during the holidays force these two best friends to forge a new appreciation for love and marriage. Susie finds herself turning over a new leaf in pursuing romance while Alec discovers love can walk into your life when you least expect it.”

title: Jenna Cold Calls Her Dad George W. Bush Live on the Air — And He Asks a Favor
summary: Jenna cold called her dad George W. Bush on TODAy and this is how the phone call went.
story: Some dads might’ve been taken off guard if their daughter spontaneously called them on live television.
Quick-thinking former President George W. Bush seized it as an opportunity to make a request instead.

The 43rd president showed off his improv skills on Sept. 17 when his daughter, TODAY’s Jenna Bush Hager, decided to call him live on the show after a request by co-host Sheinelle Jones. The call was prompted by a resurfaced clip on social media of Jenna cold-calling her father on “The Ellen DeGeneres Show” in 2007 when he was still serving as president.
“You’re on TV, Dad,” Jenna told him on TODAY.
“I’ve been trying to avoid that,” he deadpanned.

Jenna and Sheinelle then referred to the time she called him on “The Ellen DeGeneres Show” to prove that she could easily get the president on the phone. Jenna noted that Bush, 80, has still not met Sheinelle in person.
“I’d like to shake her hand, but it’s a little difficult,” he said.
Bush then learned that his administration appointed Sheinelle’s father, U.S. District Court Judge C. Darnell Jones II, in 2008.
“You got to be kidding me,” a surprised Bush said. “He had to be a good man.”
Thinking on his feet, the former president had a request for his daughter, who also happens to be the creator of the popular Read with Jenna book club.

“I’m glad you called because I don’t know if you know this or not, but I’ve got a book coming out next March,” he said. “’The Call of Freedom’s’ the name of it, and as a result of taking this call, I’m hopeful I can convince you to help me sell the book.”
“The Call of Freedom,” scheduled to be published in March 2027, is an art book featuring portraits painted by Bush of famous political prisoners from around the world.
Jenna asked if he would come on TODAY to promote the book.
“I would doubt that,” the former president said.
She said it would be a great opportunity to meet Sheinelle in person.
“I’d like to at some point in time, but why don’t you and Michelle come down...” he said.
“Sheinelle, not Michelle!” Jenna corrected while laughing.
“That’s what I meant, Sheinelle,” Bush said.
Sheinelle suggested that Jenna make “The Call of Freedom” a book club pick.
“I don’t think so, but I love you,” Jenna told her father.
Bush then cordially wrapped up the spontaneous phone call.
“Sheinelle, thank you for being such good friends with Jenna, and I wish you girls all the best,” he said.
Sheinelle complimented him on being a great dad to Jenna.
“I appreciate that very much,” he said.
After they hung up, Jenna shared her initial worry when she first surprised him with the call.
“When he said ‘I’m glad you called,’ I was like, ‘Am I grounded?’” she said to Sheinelle. “What about when he accidentally called you Michelle?”
Jenna suggested that she and Sheinelle take a road trip to her native Texas to meet the president. She also appreciated her dad’s quick thinking.
“I loved that he’s plugged his book,” she said.

title: Read The First Page of ‘Hollywood, Ending,’ The Book That Made John Green Remember: ‘I Love Writing Stories’
summary: John Green tells TODAY.com how writing his new book “Hollywood, Ending” helped him rediscover his love for storytelling. Read an excerpt.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
John Green was unsure about his place in fiction until he started working on his new book, “Hollywood, Ending.”

The novel is his first in nine years and also his first for adults. The bestselling writer behind “The Fault in Our Stars,” “Looking for Alaska” and “Paper Towns” — all of which spawned screen adaptations — hasn’t stopped writing. He most recently published the nonfiction book “Everything Is Tuberculosis” last year, and in 2021 he released a collection of personal essays called “The Anthropocene Reviewed.”
But before he made his return to fiction, Green tells TODAY.com that he “didn’t know why there needed to be another book by me in the world.”

“I had forgotten what my books were for,” he says. “I knew why I wrote nonfiction. When you write a history of tuberculosis, you’re writing as a form of social activism, as a form of advocacy. When you’re writing a novel, the motivations are a lot more complicated.”
The two-part answer came to him while crafting “Hollywood, Ending,” out Sept. 22, over a series of years.
First, he wanted to write about “how we survive” and “what we have to survive.”
“Nobody gets through this vale of tears easily,” he says.
Then, he rediscovered what he loves about his career.

“I remembered somewhere along the way of writing this book that I love writing stories,” he says. “I’ve been doing it for fun since I was 8 years old. It’s the greatest pure pleasure I’ve ever known. I love it because it allows me to escape myself. I love it because it allows me to be introverted but still talk to other people. I love it because it gives me the gift of creative expression, and I rediscovered that while writing this book. That’s a gift that I’ll carry with me for the rest of my life.”

“Hollywood, Ending” follows two rising stars named Kai Laramie and Juniper Castillo who are cast in a biopic titled “Andy Warhol Never Gets Old.” While working together, the two start to fall for each other. But they also have to navigate the challenges that come with celebrity and attempting to balance a personal and private life.

The story is told through both characters’ eyes, Green’s first time writing multiple perspectives. Green made the decision to include both voices after years of working on the novel, which altered its planned beginning, middle and end.

“It really helped me see a way into writing a bigger story. I’d never written from more than one character’s perspective before, so it was a little intimidating. But it was also kind of exciting,” he says.

He knew he had to make Juniper and Kai’s voices distinct, impacting the way they narrate their sections. He exclusively shared with TODAY.com an excerpt from the first chapter, as well as audio for the first two chapters.
The first sentence of the book reads:
When I got the news that Matthew Malone wished to make my acquaintance, I was rereading the script for "Andy Warhol Never Gets Old" in a bare-­walled apartment the studio had rented for me.
That line is from Juniper’s perspective. Just paragraphs later, Juniper and Kai meet for the first time. Green says he wrote that scene six years into the writing process.

“When you watch a rom-com, the camera turns both ways,” he says. “You see the one character, and then the camera turns around, and you see the other character. I realized I wanted the book to be like that.”
Another new experience for him was writing for an adult audience, which allowed him to tackle some “grown-up problems” he hadn’t before.
“There are still so many possibilities for the direction your life could take, which is at once wondrous and totally terrifying,” he said about exploring early adulthood.
Both Juniper and Kai have to grow up while dealing with the expectations the public has for them. Green says he leaned on some of his own feelings about his early 20s.
“I remember thinking I’m kind of living the dream, but I’m not sure I’m living my dream,” Green says.

That becomes one of the central themes of “Hollywood, Ending,” set against the backdrop of a fictional film about Andy Warhol. The influential artist and filmmaker was the “perfect foil” for the novel because he had a private and public life before it became impossible, Green says. Warhol also foresaw the importance of celebrity culture and the role screens would play in our lives, topics addressed in the book.

“I was writing another story that was about Andy Warhol called ‘Andy Warhol Never Gets Old,’” Green says. “And my wife said, ‘You should just make that into the movie (for the book). It’s so much better.’ And so I did.”

His wife has read everything he has ever written for almost 25 years, he says. She already gave her stamp of approval for “Hollywood, Ending.” Now, he waits to see how his fans will respond after nearly a decade away from fiction.
“That so many readers have that faith in my work means the world to me,” Green says.
He is nervous to see the responses — though he acknowledges that’s usually how he’s feeling.

“I think with this story in particular, I really poured my heart into it, and that’s a vulnerable thing. When an author writes a story, they should be bringing their deepest self to it. They should be vulnerable,” he says. “So that’s how I feel. It’s like all the nerve endings are on the outside of my body, and I’m just really anxious to hear how people think of it and what they respond to.”
Read the First Page of John Green’s ‘Hollywood, Ending’
Part 1
The Shoot
Juniper

When I got the news that Matthew Malone wished to make my acquaintance, I was rereading the script for ‘Andy Warhol Never Gets Old’ in a bare-­walled apartment the studio had rented for me. Matthew, I was told, wanted to meet in the lobby of his hotel. We’d all just moved to Pittsburgh, a city not known for its hotels, but Matthew had found the good one, of course. So I took an Uber there, pounding Altoids the whole way, thinking about what I’d say to the one and only Matthew Malone, who was playing Warhol in the movie. Matthew and I had exchanged phone calls and a couple of text messages, but my friends all wanted to know what he smelled like, how he walked, what kind of emotion his eyes held, whether or not he was a typical Pisces, and so on.

The first time we talked, a few months after my mother died, he called me and said, “I’m so excited to work with you on this,” and I said, “Me too,” and then he said, “I know you’ve been crossing through a hard time, and I’m sorry.” What a phrase. Crossing through a hard time. I was indeed crossing through a hard time.

In the first weeks after Mom died, I mostly felt relief that it was over. I felt like I was coming up for air after a long time underwater. But eventually, I learned that it was not, in fact, over. The dead are not in the past, not really, because you carry them around with you.
